He presents a facade of ignorance and subtle stupidity, letting his eagerness manifest in his demeanour as an indistinct ‘shakiness,' professing that he hasn’t been right since the explosion. At all times, he attempts to engender sympathy for his situation and tries to appear unthreatening to avoid suspicion.

Kathor Navrak

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.kdhQ2SwO7Vm2rzUI description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Kathor Navrak}

Roleplaying Kathor Navrak

Kathor Navrak’s monolithic ambition is enough to outweigh anything as delicate as guilt or pity, underpinned by his burning desire to emulate the highborn nobles who cast him out. The characters come face to face with Navrak in the climax, where, despite their intrusion and discovery of his operation, he meets their advances with the utmost confidence and certainty of his own forces’ success. This has rubbed off even on the gangers who serve him — despite their loyalty being owed to other figures within the Knives, many have begun to believe Navrak’s proclamations that long and easy lives can be their’s, so long as he is given everything he requires.

Lerna Harrog

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.i1LNkpV6WWiZR7PL description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

Roleplaying Lerna Harrog

Lerna Harrog has been following the party since their visit to the ruins of Manufactorum Vitus-II, moving through the mass of twisting tunnels and conduits running throughout the hive. She barely remembers her life before, and indeed, what Humanity she still possesses is fading fast. Though she volunteered to test the Vylathi Knives' woeful attempts at rejuvenat treatment, she hardly understood the risks she was undertaking. Powerful mutagenic chemicals have wracked her body, warping her mind and flesh alike. 

Harrog seeks revenge and hopes the party can help her get it. But make no mistake — Harrog is no longer Human; the longer she lives, the more monstrous she becomes.

Tech-Priest Tybaris Arx

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.PrUAoOrVdfD1HcAx description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

Skitarii Forces

Pressured by the nobility of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} to investigate the destruction of Manufactorum Vitus-II, while protecting the secrets of their rejuvenat formulas, the Magi of Forge Fane Incalcos-6 decided to deploy their maniple of Skitarii Vanguard to cut to the heart of the investigation. Efficient and cold, rather than overtly callous, the Vanguard, led by their Alpha, Landa-12, have never failed an operation they have been sent to resolve.

Rarely deployed unless absolutely necessary, Skitarii Vanguard are infused with radiation, emitting a debilitating aura they themselves are inured to. This hardens them to fight in the most toxic war zones, including the destroyed Vitus-II, to defend the Forge Fane’s interests.

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.vsiOALilPnEe3dKg description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.jSJkugzVGrfqbl9o description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

Grafted Ganger

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ciU9gLyQG3bdXpT1 description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

pages.name: Interminable Devotion
pages.text: Fear and suspicion mount amongst a skeleton crew of distrustful souls toiling together within a venerable Capitol Imperialis while an underhanded enemy sets sinister plans in motion. Interminable Devotion is an adventure that can be used as a stand-alone experience, spanning 2–4 sessions or as a part of a larger campaign. Be sure to familiarise yourself with the various @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg]{Dramatis Personae}, as their interactions and confrontations with the party are key to how this adventure evolves.

pages.name: Adventure Overview
pages.text:
The auto quill scratches fitfully on the bone-white page as Curator Varness reviews the reports for the thirteenth time in two hours, yet the details remain the same. Then there are the picts, but she can’t deny them, though she’s tried. Having ruled out distortion, grime on the lens and atmospheric interference, she’s left with a single regretful conclusion: they’re real. As she scrubs all but a select few from the archive, acid rain lashes the narrow armaglass windows of her cramped quarters aboard the Interminable Devotion, beyond which the rolling fortresses’ harsh lumens reveal an expanse of inhospitable wasteland, corrosive fog and acidic devastation.

Designed for a party of low to moderately advanced characters, Interminable Devotion combines mystery, horror and investigation elements to tell a story of murder, conspiracy and familial hatreds. The party is tasked by their Patron to investigate a secretive research mission and soon find themselves pulled into the thick of a mysterious string of murders aboard an ancient Capitol Imperialis traversing Voll’s acidic wasteland.

@UUID[.gqWQ8LhVWHKBodFY]{Part 1: The Brunt of Voll} — After reaching the Interminable Devotion, the party discovers Captain Alarad Veridian’s corpse. Initially suspected of murder, they are soon vindicated and meet with Curator Varness, now the highest-ranking officer aboard the Devotion. After telling them about strange happenings, she charges them with finding the killer.

@UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR]{Part 2: Scrutiny and Suspicion} — The party begins their investigation, exploring the Devotion and talking to NPCs to uncover clues. As they progress, they’ll find new clues to help them solve the mystery, uncovering a dangerous chemical agent before building towards the final confrontation with the adventure’s villain, Vesterick Nethecaré. 

@UUID[.8OWiZxbLaURKKVKb]{Part 3: A Mind in Ruins} — Armed now with a trove of information, the party returns to the Curator and makes their case, only for calamity to erupt as a concentrated form of Vesterick Nethecaré’s agent is released aboard the Devotion. Upon making their way through the maddened decks, the characters must pursue the noble into the wasteland for the last confrontation.

@UUID[.MbWSJCh5GLhtUKvE]{Aftermath} — With Vesterick Nethecaré defeated and his plan foiled, the party may recover or destroy the formula for the noxious chemical agent he had used upon the crew. Upon returning to the Devotion, the party calls for extraction. 

Vesterick Nethecaré

Vesterick Nethecaré was born into a decrepit, precarious branch of the vaulted House Nethecaré, the family name, while enough to raise him above the teeming filth and grant him a life amongst the smog-choked spires of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal}, it granted him little else. His young life was tense, ever wondering if the rest of the brood might tire of his family’s drain on the Nethecaré coffers and see fit instead to prune them. Yet this all changed with the death of his father. 

Hundar Nethecaré left to attend a meeting and never returned. Despite a body never surfacing, he was swiftly declared dead, and a cursory memorial followed. After the mandatory mourning period was observed, Vesterick Nethecaré’s mother was quickly married to Gruledis Nethecaré — his grand-uncle from his father’s side of the family. Technically, this was a vast leap in status for the lesser noble and his mother, but his grand-uncle’s heirs ensured Vesterick Nethecaré never forgot the stain he was on the Nethecaré name. This atmosphere of ridicule and derision pushed the young man to work tirelessly to prove his worth and master the House trade. No gene went unmapped or cell unturned from the meagre remnants he was permitted to work with. Years passed without success, yet everything changed the night of the test. 

Bitter and frustrated at the stark variables presented by his test thralls, the noble took rash action, injecting himself with an unknown concoction of potent hallucinogens and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }pheromones. The room spun, his perceptions reeled, he stumbled and fell as strange noises and hallucinations began to scurry and flutter in his periphery. Then he saw a vision.

Vesterick Nethecaré gasped as, amongst the melting walls, crawling things and disembodied laughter, a twisted figure emerged, Human flesh mingled with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi} biology, yet the face was unmistakable; it was his father. 

Vesterick Nethecaré fell back in horror, yet the monstrous revenant pushed forward, mandibles clacking so close to his face that he could smell the reeking spittle, then he began to speak. Several hours later, Vesterick Nethecaré awoke to his lab in ruins. He and his equipment lay broken, notes were scattered, and his hands were bloody, yet one thing caught his eye above all else. On the floor, written in blood, was a nearly complete chemical formula, one he believed allowed him to commune with the dead.

But he knew the formula needed more testing and resources than the house would allow. In his father’s notes, he learned about the Interminable Devotion and how it had fallen under the sway of the chem guild in their ongoing expeditions, and as a source of collecting the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }pheromone that his formula required. Vesterick Nethecaré saw an opportunity; he would go right to the source and continue his experiments far from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} in an enclosed environment. He would perfect his formula, commune with his father again, and show House Nethecaré his worth.

The Last Living Castle

The Interminable Devotion, a retrofitted Capitol Imperialis, grinds through Voll’s acid wastes on tracks large enough to crush buildings to dust. It currently shelters hundreds of souls deployed on a privately funded research mission. The veteran engine has a long history dating back to the Macharian Crusade — it was initially deployed as a mobile fortress for Imperial Knights and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} walker squads who hunted the planet’s once abundant strains of colossal @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. It could withstand the brunt of their monstrous attacks, provide ample artillery support, and transport their prized carcasses for study.

Even with the decline in colossal @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, the Interminable Devotion still soldiers on across the wastes, surveying spawning grounds for signs of reemergence and catching strains for research. Some among the crew think it has been lost somewhere in the Departmento Munitorum’s records, or, while revered as an engine of war, deemed too burdensome to transport off Voll to a new battlefront. However, they still recognise how much of an honour it is to serve on such an ancient Imperialis.

Centuries exposed to Voll’s rigours have not been kind to its internal workings. Despite recent and arcane maintenance rites performed by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} personnel regarding its environmental systems, many lie marred beyond repair. Perhaps worst of all is the inert macrocannon that juts at its zenith, the once-impressive armament serving as a symbol of power now lost to the ages. Yet even so, the mobile fortress is far from defenceless. Stalling due to engine failure or track damage is a constant threat, but there is little short of concentrated heavy ordinance that can pose the Devotion serious peril from the outside. Inside, however, is another matter entirely.

Chemical Communion

‘Through snaking pipelines and rusted vents, Vesterick Nethecaré’s chemical communion slithers its gaseous form through the Devotions bones, infiltrating every passage, occupying every chamber as vast as the Hangar, as minute as the smallest runoff grate, a hidden spectre, invisible and everywhere’.

This potent nerve agent, rendered from toxic fungi, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }pheromones and refined neural secretions quietly builds in the subject’s system, inducing paranoia and conjuring disturbing hallucinations before culminating in explosions of apoplectic violence. The Interminable Devotion possesses a bespoke filtration and air supply system to combat Voll’s hazardous environment — the perfect place, so contained and off the grid, for the noble to experiment with his chemical communion.

Mixed with the standard oxygen supply, the chemical communion is impossible to detect on any craft systems, and there is no central source for any curious menial to blunder into. Vesterick Nethecaré himself has tampered with the equipment aboard to avoid any interference. For example, all rebreathers and protective gear aboard have been carefully and undetectably damaged to ensure the crew’s exposure. Despite preventative measures, tar-like build-ups have congealed in the Devotions’ air filters. Should a character possess the knowledge or tools to analyse this substance, they may attempt a Hard (+20) Logic (Investigation) Test. If they succeed, inform them of the following:

CLUE: The residue appears to have congealed from an airborne substance synthesised from acynadi pheromones. An extended analysis with lab equipment would be required to unravel its secrets fully. However, it’s likely to have hallucinogenic properties. It’s pretty likely this substance has been leaking outside the Devotion. This could account for much of the strange acynadi behaviour surrounding the craft.

Vesterick Nethecaré believes his deceased father has supplied the formula for his chemical communion and that he can commune with him while under its hallucinogenic effects. The noble has built up a tolerance to the communion, allowing him to withstand constant mild exposure while aboard the Devotion. Additionally, he has devised grenades that hold a concentrated form of the communion along with syringes loaded with a similar liquid solution. 

Contamination

During the adventure, the party is passively exposed to Vesterick Nethecaré’s chemical communion via the Devotions' air supply. Ask the characters to make Fortitude Tests at various points in the adventure (do not invoke the Poison specialisation as it might give the game away!). The following list covers some suggested points in the narrative to ask for these Tests, but it rather depends on how long your characters spend on the Interminable Devotion trying to figure out the mystery.

  • At the end of Part 1 (when the party is detained in the brig).

  • After they have investigated a few locations in Part 2.

  • After they have investigated a few more locations in Part 2 (see @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#time-for-communion]{Time for Communion}).

  • As they race through the Devotion in Part 3.

As their exposure to the chemical increases, the Difficulty of these Fortitude Tests also increases.

  • During Part 1: Routine (+20)

  • During Part 2: Challenging (+0) 

  • During Part 3: Hard (−20) 

Among the characters who fail these Tests, choose someone who rolled the least SL. They experience some form of auditory or visual hallucination. See the Auditory Hallucinations and Visual Hallucinations Tables for some ideas for what characters could experience under the effects of contamination — but any of these suggestions can be improved by adding aspects of NPCs who are important to the characters, especially anyone who has passed away; family, friends, lost comrades and the like (much like how Vesterick Nethecaré saw visions of his dead father when first exposed).

Furthermore, any character who fails two of these Tests in a row begins to suffer severely from the chemical communion. They effectively have the Fatigued Condition, rolling all Tests with Disadvantage, until they can breathe clean air once more (either by fixed breathing apparatus, spending time outside the Devotion, or fixing Vesterick Nethecaré’s sabotage of the air systems).

pages.name: Getting Started
pages.text:
The adventure begins with their Patron’s briefing on the mission — they are provided with initial information on the expedition and their motivations for sending them to investigate. Their Patron also supplies them with the following equipment to aid them in their adventure. 

Extreme Weather Clothing

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-items.Item.zyIQkeHkEhcRn2Gu]{Extreme Weather Clothing} grants the wearer +1 SL on Fortitude (Endurance) Tests to resist the types of extreme weather the clothing is designed to protect against. In this instance, they are provided with coverings and cloaks that protect them from Voll's acidic rainfall and atmosphere.

The party has an opportunity to gather anything they require before departing, but their Patron insists they must leave before the end of the day. They have been provided with aerial transport to reach the last known coordinates of the expedition — if they are in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, their transport departs from the mid-levels of the Void Buttress.

A few hours after takeoff, nearing the landing site, their flight encounters a savage storm that has swallowed the area, complicating their landing.

Patrons

Understanding the players’ Patron’s involvement in seeking out the Interminable Devotion is key to kicking off the adventure. Below are suggested motivations for each Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: Your Patron has received word that several archives have been redacted without proper authorisation. Further digging has uncovered fragmented information that, when pieced together, points to a private Nethecaré expedition into Voll’s wilderness. This breach of protocol must be investigated. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: Your Patron has encountered strange fragments of disturbing beastial imagery clinging to the astropathic currents near Voll’s wastes. The source of this interference must be determined. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: Your Patron has uncovered evidence of a Capitol Imperialis at work on Voll, upon cross-referencing its idents with Mechanicum records, the engine was designated killed in action over a century ago; the fate of such a relic must be confirmed. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: Your Patron has received intel about a Nethecaré noble who claimed they can speak to the dead. This man, one Vesterick Nethecaré, has recently departed @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} on a secretive research mission. Whatever madness is at hand affronts the God-Emperor’s Holy Ministorum.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: Your Patron has heard rumours that several deserters have formed a mercenary company on Voll. After applying the correct pressure, it was uncovered that the deserters' ringleader, a man named Drukos, is stationed aboard a secretive Nethecaré research craft. This coward must face the God-Emperor’s justice for his crimes.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: Your Patron has intercepted a short-wave vox message cast out into the void. While heavily corrupted with vox distortion, a ‘Captain Alrad Veridian’ requests immediate extraction from an isolated region of Voll, providing specific coordinates.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: Your Patron has received a tip on the whereabouts of a former associate who cleaned out three gambling dens and skipped planet with the winnings. The cheater has acquired false papers under the name ‘Hinji’, working for a shady Nethecaré research expedition in Voll’s wastes. Find him and settle the score; the house never loses. 

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: The Inquisition’s eyes and ears have collated many rumours regarding rogue Nethecaré chemists and supposed prophets who can speak to the dead — this all reeks of heresy, and it all points to the wayward Capitol Imperialis.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasties}: Your Patron’s curiosity has been stoked upon discovering records of rare chemicals changing hands tied to a secretive Nethecaré research mission. Investigate this curio, and recover anything that might be of value. 

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: Discover whoever leads this secretive mission, put them down for their deceit, and set the Interminable Devotion back to its regular patrol.

  • Information: Such a well-occluded expedition must surely have valuable secrets. Retrieve all data on the expedition's elusive goal and its findings.

  • Materiel: Such a shady expedition is likely to have brought in any number of valuable resources off record, not to mention their objective. Secure any notable assets for future use. 

  • Reputation: Expose this secretive expedition so that others think twice before attempting such clandestine operations. 

  • Unity: If others expose this expedition’s underhanded nature, it will only create further distrust; investigate and resolve it quietly to avoid potential conflict.

pages.name: Part 1: The Brunt of Voll
pages.text:
The danger of the storm is apparent; attempting to fly through it would tempt death. However, vast eyes in the storm are observable, forming sizable islands of calm in the otherwise raging atmosphere. One is not far from the coordinates their Patron provided. This is the safest chance at reaching the surface intact.

Braving the Weather

‘The lander settles down upon the uneven surface and promptly sinks several feet into the mud below. Around you, an expanse of fetid acidic marshland stretches out to meet the borders of the swiftly approaching storm.’

The party is then confronted with obstacles on their journey to the Interminable Devotion. As they progress, take note of the SL of each roll they make, adding the party’s positive SLs together and subtracting negative SLs from the total. Upon reaching their destination, if the total is 6 SL or more, the party avoids obtaining the Fatigued (Minor) Condition. 

‘Exiting the lander, the storm engulfs you, smothering all natural light and leaving you to traverse the acidic marshland in storm-choked darkness. The howling wind and torrential acid rain lash you terribly, forcing you between jagged rock formations that quickly become labyrinthine.’

In this first challenge, characters must succeed on a Routine (+20) Awareness (Sight) Test with Advantage if they are working together as a group. Characters who fail take [[/r 1d10]] Damage from jagged rocks as they wander in the storm. 

CLUE: The characters with the most SL on the Awareness Test notice that these rock formations more closely resemble ruins, with markings and signs of structure evident.

'The terrain around you narrows into a sharp gully flanked by sheer cliffs on either side. Though sheltered from the wind, a strange mist thickens, and you soon come to a significant circular depression at least twenty feet across in which a caustic green liquid bubbles.'

In this second challenge, the party must succeed on a Challenging (+0) Athletics (Running) Test to jump over the depression. If a character fails, they suffer [[/r 1d10]] Damage from landing in the exceptionally corrosive substance.

'As the gully opens out once more, the wind howls in a terrible keening roar and from a ridge to your left dozens of terrified and disoriented acynadi spill over in a chaotic stampede, their alien forms flailing with barbs, spines and claws.'

In this third challenge, the party must succeed on a Routine (+20) Stealth (Move Silently) Test to avoid the frantic creatures; should any of them fail, two large @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5} attack them. 

'In a flash of lightning, the characters notice a colossal shadow on the far side of the ridge. It seems like a hill, then it begins to move, sinking back into the darkness of the storm. As you recover from the acynadi stampede, you see it, standing out in the black gulf of storm-wracked wasteland. A bank of lights, yet even at this distance, its source is clear. The Interminable Devotion.'

The party makes their last push through the open to reach the Devotion. If any character suffered 7 or more Damage from the three challenges, they receives the Poisoned (Minor) Condition, and their extreme weather clothing has been damaged to the point it no longer protects them from the toxic conditions. Also count up their total SL from all three challenges and inflict them with the Fatigued (Minor) Condition as previously described.

Read or paraphrase the following:

’A mobile fortress, ancient and colossal towers before you. A retrofitted Capitol Imperialis, the Interminable Devotion boasts fifty-meter-high battlements, potent weaponry and tracks large enough to level small buildings. Its huge disembarkation ramp yawns open before you.’

Safe Harbour

Upon entering the Hangar, the party finds that the heavy lumens have been deactivated. The massive hangar door is open, and an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-requisition-actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter} is visible nearby. Should they investigate the Hangar further, they discover the corpse of Captain Alard Veridian. Read aloud or paraphrase the following:

‘Slumped against a storage locker, you see the body of an ageing man in a large pool of blood, a discarded laspistol at his side. His pale, bloodless features locked in silent terror above his utterly crushed throat.’

Immediately, the sound of an opening bulkhead accompanies heavy bootsteps. @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos} and ten of his mercenaries enter the Hangar (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Trooper} stat-block to represent them. Drukos first asks the party if they are the work detail. But upon noticing the body, he and his men become aggressive, demanding they hand over their weapons before placing them under arrest for the murder of Captain Alrad Veridian.

The party is escorted to an ex-storage cabin turned brig, where @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos} questions them about the murder. Initially suspicious of the characters, he soon begins to believe their story but keeps them in the brig under heavy guard until he can investigate. As they leave, the massive hangar ramp retracts, and the Interminable Devotion gets back underway.

What happened?

During a routine medicae check, Medicae Roderick (or rather @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}) took the opportunity to secretly inject the Captain with his latest batch of his concentrated @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. Driven by visions and paranoia, the Captain called for the Interminable Devotion to a complete stop, and attempted to leave alone on the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-requisition-actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighter} they keep for emergencies. 

Having bugged Captain Veridian to monitor the effects of his formula, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} was forewarned of his plan, and he intercepted the Captain in the Hangar, accompanied by one of his Medicae Servitors. He ordered the Servitor to kill the Captain to cover his tracks, then to hide the murder weapon, subsequently ordered the Servitor to disappear into the wastes while the Devotion was stationary. The noble managed to return to the Medicae Ward without being noticed.

Hours pass, allowing the party to rest before Drukos returns, where he informs the party that they are cleared of his suspicions. The Devotion’s augur scans detected their landing craft, and the adepts’ medicae report states time of death as just before they touched down. Drukos then tells them that @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} wants to speak with them and leads them to the Curator’s Quarters. Once inside, she asks the party for their account while dismissing @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}. With him gone, she promptly states the following. 

‘Peculiar occurrences have been reported and duly suppressed for several weeks now. Strange reports of seeing frightful things aboard, distorted acynadi that look partly Human. This is ludicrous; the reporters have been disciplined and told to keep quiet. But the reports keep coming in, and they are all so similar. Then there’s the picts.’ The @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator} turns her cogitator display to show a pict of hundreds of acynadi lying still, just beyond the edge of the Devotion’s heavy lumens. ‘They seem to be flocking or gathering and following the Devotion as if waiting for something…’

‘I have suppressed the reports and the picts as much as possible to avoid hysteria amongst the crew, yet now with the murder of the Captain, something needs to be done. You seem like capable individuals, and seeing as you arrived after the murder, you are the only ones beyond my suspicion. So, as acting commander of this expedition, I’m charging you with spearheading this investigation. Whatever you find, you are to come to me here and present your evidence before I will authorise the use of any force. The last thing we want is a bloodbath.’

The party receives a handheld vox, the authority to question the crew and any previously confiscated weapons. If any characters are unarmed, they are given two common weapons of their choice from the Devotion’s armoury (Imperium Maledictum). @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} suggests beginning with the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#a1.-hangar]{crime scene}, the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b1.-the-medicae-ward]{Medicae Ward} or asking around in @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b2.-the-mess]{the Mess}.

pages.name: Part 2: Scrutiny and Suspicion
pages.text:
The characters can now explore the decks and interact with the Devotion’s various NPCs, piecing together initial clues and suspicions. There is no set path for the order of the investigation. As clues are discovered, the scenarios provided trigger, each providing the party with an additional clue to help solve the mystery.

Remember that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} has rigged the Devotion’s air supply with his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, and has bugged many of the key locations and NPCs across the Capitol Imperialis to keep an ear on the key members of the crew and observe the effects of his chemical communion from afar, which means he can often stay one step ahead of the characters once they are aboard.

The Interminable Devotion

The Capitol Imperialis is arranged into three primary decks from bottom to top.

A. Enginarium Deck — (bottom) the Hangar and primary engines.

B. Habitation Deck — (middle) the Barracks and other crew services.

C. Militarum Deck — (top) the Bridge and other administrative cabins.

Throughout the decks are plentiful gun emplacements and battlements. Not listed but still worth considering is the topmost deck located above the Militarum Deck. This deck consists of the upper battlements, where the macrocannon sits (currently needing extensive repair), a small observation nest, and a landing pad for flyers.

Throughout the Capitol Imperialis, the interior is constantly tight, like the innards of a voidship, with plenty of turns and overhangs that characters can hit their heads on. The Hangar is the largest open space aboard, multi-levelled and accessed externally from the front or the rear of the Imperialis. It can hold multiple tanks, walkers, and even flyers simultaneously.

A. Enginarium Deck

Flickering red lumens dully illuminate a snaking labyrinth of steaming pipes, ribbed cables and coolant tubes, as footsteps of servitors and menials alike echo metallically from the walkways and gantries beyond.

Sections of the Interminable Devotion’s engines are spread across this deck, bisected by the massive multi-tiered central hangar. Tightly packed engines and constructs constantly whirr and strain, spitting out steam and crackles of electricity — the servitors at work are programmed to ignore the obvious hazard, but the party should be well advised to keep their hands at their sides while passing through.

A1. Hangar

Towering crates and stacks of steel barrels form a series of high walls around lines of metal storage lockers where data slates stand racked in steel housing.

The Hangar is a huge bulk storage area buried in the dimly lit guts of the Devotion’s Enginarium Deck. Where once the grind of battle tanks and the lockstep of guardsmen echoed in the space, the Hangar is now an area that few frequent and those that must, do so swiftly. The sound of footfalls resounds loudly on the metal decking, and the towering walls of supplies cast thick shadows. The party can find a reliquary of data slates. If they inspect the data, they uncover the following clue. 

CLUE: The records state that a locker was accessed just before the Captain’s estimated time of death. Inside is a small bloodstained data coil. Upon loading it into a cogitator, they find a report requesting the termination of the expedition, stating initial reconnaissance data was falsified, implicating the initials ‘V.N.’ along with copies of official documents tallying losses from a battle forty years ago. These include a record of the destruction of a Capitol Imperialis designated the ‘Interminable Devotion’.

If the party examines other data slate entries for anything unusual, they can make a Routine (+20) Tech (Security) Test. Upon success, supply them with the following clue.

CLUE: A particular report details a recent withdrawal. It is notated and logged on the supply manifest as a withdrawal of ink and parchment. However, only the stores of pain meds and bandages have been reduced. Someone has been stealing medical supplies.

If the party inspects or takes items stored within the Hangar, they find it well stocked with stacks of tools and clothing of Common availability (Imperium Maledictum). Should any characters look for weapons or armour, they find none stored within the Hangar, as all such items are firmly locked within the armoury on the Militarum Deck. 

A2. Central Cogitarum 

Pale-faced scribes and grotesque servitors hunch over banks of cogitators and auspex scanners underlit by the harsh blue light of their instruments. Curator Varness’s imposing command throne looms over a large holographic display, projecting the wasteland beyond the Devotion’s walls.

Embedded near the Devotion’s core, the Central Cogitarum never sleeps. As a facility wholly dedicated to information storage and exchange, this feretory is where most of the expedition’s data is enshrined. Should a character inspect one of the cogitators, they can open and examine several different archives, as follows.

Personnel Files

The party quickly finds that many of these are incomplete, with whole areas missing, and many are marked with a seal bearing the initials ‘V.N.’ Characters can make a Routine (+20) Logic (Investigation) Test to reveal the following clue. 

CLUE: You soon uncover inconsistencies that strongly suggest the files surrounding Drukos and his men are forgeries, along with patchy service records that imply a former militarum affiliation. 

Initial Survey Data

The expedition’s initial survey data is an archive of the original data supplied to justify the mission. It details vast @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }population numbers, tolerable climate pH levels and theories of surviving infrastructure. Glancing over this data reveals the following clue.

CLUE: It quickly becomes clear to the party that this information is so blatantly incorrect that it is likely to have been intentionally falsified. 

Pict Records

Inside the Devotion’s pict store, the party finds a horde of grainy images depicting misty acidic marshland and strange desolate ruins. However, something becomes apparent as they flip through them and gain the following clue.

CLUE: Flipping through the picts you notice images of the same locations captured at different time stamps. However, the landscape seems to change dramatically in some of the picts with a large dark hill appearing out of the mist time and time again, almost as if it were following the Devotion. 

If characters question any of the scribes about the strange information contained within the records, many admit that they had noticed the same irregularities. However, it is not within their remit to question superiors, but they have inquired about the strange pictures. Despite the honesty of this statement, the party gets a sense that they are holding something back. They can make a Routine (+20) Rapport (Inquiry) Test to gain the following clue.

CLUE: The scribes unwittingly or maliciously reveal that they believe Curator Varness is underqualified for her post and, as a result, has been unable to perform her duties to a routine standard.

A3. The Artificery

Large steel tables support several workstations where incomplete servitor arms and other more unrecognisable devices lie strewn. Racked banks of cogitators display complex graphs and binaric readouts while loose chains and thick steel hoists hang from the chamber ceiling in a foliage of rusted metal.

In the guts of the Enginarium Deck lies the personal quarters of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49}, the Devotions’ sole Tech-Priest. Effectively a shrine to the Omnissiah, the crew generally regards it as something more akin to a repair station, much to Mathus-49’s chagrin. Characters can use this area and the tools available to repair or maintain their equipment, but the Tech-Priest will surely approach them if they linger too long.

B. Habitation Deck

Cold lumens punctuate the gloomy corridors with harsh white beams as the drunken clamour echoes from off-duty crew. Behind closed doors, the cramped crew cabins are packed with stacked bunks bearing the rust and acidic stains of decades of service.

The Habitation Deck consists of staff and barrack cabins, mostly cramped cabins stuck between blocks of machinery and battlements, where most of the crew spend most of their time off duty.

B1. The Medicae Ward

The smell of antiseptic gels and coagulants saturates your nostrils with a stinging tang. Against the left wall, a dozen beds are laid out upon a grimy tile floor set with rusting drains. A brown plastic curtain partially covers a narrow passage through which a surgical table and medical supplies are visible.

If this is the party’s first time entering the ward, they find @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick} and his attendants finishing a bloody amputation. If this is their first time meeting him, the medicae will introduce himself. Ushering them into his surgical theatre, Captain Veridian’s corpse is laid out under a sheet. If the party asks about the autopsy, Medicare Roderick truthfully corroborates his adept’s findings — it appears the Captain died from his crushed throat, inflicted by some mechanical tool. However, he has only given the body a cursory once-over himself, with a complete autopsy to be performed in time. He also informs the party that the Captain’s effects are in a box on the shelf. Roderick then excuses himself to attend to his other patients.

Should the party wish to examine the Captain’s corpse, they may attempt a Routine (+20) Medicae (Human) Test. If they succeed, they are supplied with the following additional clues. 

CLUE: Upon examining the body, the party discovers shredded pieces of flesh beneath the Captain’s fingernails, whether his own or someone else’s, it cannot be deduced. 

CLUE: Furthermore, you discover what appears to be a small bruise on the Captain's arm, indicative of an injection site. 

If Roderick is informed of these details, he scolds his adepts and servitors for their foolishness and compliments the characters for their diligence. 

Should the party wish to examine the Captain’s effects, they find a heavily stained yet unremarkable @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} uniform, a pair of boots and a silver ring.

If the characters want to search the rest of the Medicae Ward for clues, they may attempt a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test. Upon success, supply them with the following clue. 

CLUE: Looking through the various files and cabinets, you find a book that doesn’t fit. This tome is bound in the finest polished leather, its pages gilded with glittering gold edges. Inside, you find flowing embellished script forming a strange dialect of High Gothic. If a character has the Linguistics (High Gothic) Specialisation, they discover it is a historical text detailing the family tree of House Nethecaré. If questioned, Medicae Roderick states that he has a great interest in the histories of Volls' noble families, particularly house Nethecaré, as he does have a distant familial connection to the house.

Should the party scrutinise @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick} further, a character can attempt a Challenging (+0) Intuition (People) Test. On a success, they suspect that he is withholding something. 

B2. The Mess

‘The bitter odour of stale grog hangs heavy in the air, and though the mugs are rusted and the lumens flicker, it’s the only place on the Devotion with any sense of levity. A scattering of stools surrounds oblong tables leading up to a corroded counter that stretches the length of the far wall.’

The mess hall, colloquially dubbed ‘the Mess’ by many of the crew, has become more akin to a drinkery than its intended purpose of doling out calculated portions of nutrient-middling paste. This is due to the under-the-table sale of rotgut booze fermented in a crew cabin lavatory by @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#menial-boris]{Boris} and a few of his close associates. As a result, it has become a popular spot and one of the few places where personnel mix. This can take the shape of exchanging tall tales or playing cards. The party may encounter the following short interactions while in the Mess.

Tall Tales

The party notices a group of menials sitting at a corner table in the Mess. Wide eyes darting in their pale faces. Should the party approach them, they cease their discussion, only resuming when they have left. If the party succeeds on a Challenging (+0) Stealth (Move Silently) Test to approach the table without being noticed or a Routine (+20) Awareness (Sound) Test, they hear the following clue.

CLUE: ‘It just appeared out of nowhere, I was coming back from the Hangar and the damned lumens went out, then it got ice cold and I turned around and there he was. An old fella, pale as death, but all wrong, with pincers and mandibles like an acynadi, he tried to say something, but I ran for it. When the lights came back, I turned around and he was gone.’

Dagger Counts

Dagger Counts is a deception-based card game that has become popular amongst the crew. Should any characters wish to play, bets of credits or objects of value are accepted. Once this is agreed, the game can begin. Each round, players must choose an appropriate Skill and make a Test, providing a plausible narrative reason for the Skill they chose, at your discretion. For example, a character may use Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) to try and deftly swipe an extra card or Intuition (People) to try and read other players’ bluffs, or Rapport (Deception) to bluff themselves. Characters must stick to using their chosen Skill throughout the game.

Difficulty increases each round of play, and the number of rounds played equals the number of characters plus the number of NPCs involved. Typically, use three NPCs plus any number of characters who wish to play. In the first round, Tests are made at Routine (+20) Difficulty, then Challenging (+0), and then Hard (−20), and so on. For the NPCs, roll for them as a group and assume they are using a Logic (Evaluation) Skill of 30 to play.

At the end of a round, eliminate the character or one of the NPCs who rolled the least SL. Once all rounds have been completed, the winner remains and claims the prize pot (decide for yourself among the NPCs if there is a tie).

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} is undefeated at Dagger Counts, and many have learned the hard way not to play him. This is due to his latent psychic talent giving him an edge, without him even knowing it. You may include this as a topic of discussion or include Old Hinji in the game — if you do, simply fabricate his rolls behind the GM screen to always succeed.

The following clue is revealed at the end of a game of Dagger Counts, in which characters took part, observed, or if they are just passing through the Mess.

CLUE: As the game of Dagger Counts ends, the bickering mingles with the general cacophony of the Mess. Then Old Hinji collapses, convulsing violently, silencing the din. As he comes around, a sudden nosebleed splashes his overalls, appearing as if he had a grisly gut wound. He looks at the cards strewn around the floor and seems somewhere far away before he faints. ‘Ruins… it’ll all end in ruins’. 

If the characters do not bring Old Hinji to the Medicae Ward (B1), some of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos}’ goons in the Mess pick him up and drag him there for treatment.

B3. The Agri-Chamber

‘Lit by the dim glow of a single cogitator screen and the sharp crimson glimmer of servitor eye-lenses, fungal spores germinate in banks of slender armaglass chambers. Nearby, grim rendering vats sit idle as if ready for their next meal.’

Despite occupying a meagre portion of the Habitation Deck, the Agri-Chamber squats all too close to the Mess, yet despite this close proximity, it is a shunned place. The operation produces a daily ration of nutrient-rich paste for each crew member to supplement the expedition’s standard supplies and aid in preventing diseases caused by dietary insufficiencies. Grimly, this is also where the bodies of any deceased crew are brought, with each body providing ample nutrition for many generations of fungal spores. The only regular visitors are the servitors who operate it. 

B4. Crew Quarters

‘Parallel corridors of corrosion and peeling paint bear heavy sliding doors that give way to the quarters within. Dozens of bunks are stacked end over end beyond which metal floored ablutions chambers waft their damp odour.’

Forming the vast majority of the Habitation Deck, the crew quarters are where the vast majority of all personnel aboard the Devotion take their allotted rest. While no precise edicts govern crew distribution amongst these chambers, particular cliques have staked their claim on singular areas. This has resulted in the scribes and menials clustering and shunning those they perceive as outsiders. Rumour has it that @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#menial-boris]{Boris }and a few of his compatriots are using one of the ablution chambers to ferment rot-gut booze. 

C. Militarum Deck

‘Within the mouldering halls of the Militarum Deck the epitaph of the Devotion’s past glories rot for all to see. The cold metal faces of martyred commanders and imperial saints stare out from the walls in low relief. Their blank eyes spilling tears of orange and teal oxide, drowning names and deeds in a sorrow of corrosion.’

The Militarum Deck contains all the command and administration cabins for the Interminable Devotion, and access to the top deck of the Capitol Imperialis (upper battlements, macrocannon, observation nest, and landing pad). 

C1. The Hall of Remembrance

‘The coldness of the Militarum Deck plummets to new lows as freezing air fogs all breath. The chamber walls are bedecked with decrepit tapestries commemorating the Devotion’s past battles. Six iron pillars run floor to ceiling in mimicry of ancient Terran monuments, while a huge central tapestry dominates the space, depicting lines of heroic guardsmen laying a horde of traitors low.’

The Hall of Remembrance lingers near the head of the Militarum Deck, and many avoid passing the chamber whenever they can. Though few dare speak of it, weeping is sometimes heard from the hall, often accompanied by the distant clash of blades and screaming.

This strange phenomenon is centred around the chamber’s largest and oldest tapestry, depicting the Devotion’s landfall on Voll and subsequent battles against the planet’s larger @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, which rival the Devotion in size and stature. The truth comes from a mix of the crew’s paranoia under the effect of the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} and how it stokes @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji’}s latent powers due to his long-term exposure to the chemical. While Old Hinji is present in the hall, some of these aspects take an audible and visible form, giving off a fearful and uncomfortable aura.

The characters can discover the following clue if Old Hinji is not accompanying them.

CLUE: Upon entering the hall, the party gets the unmistakable feeling they are being watched. Soon, they notice a figure out of place in the large central tapestry. Amongst the Astra Militarum forces, an elderly man stands, his eyes sharp and terrible, his face a horrific amalgamation of Human and acynadi features.

The characters can make a Routine (+20) Awareness (Sight) Test to inspect the other tapestries. If successful, provide them with the following clue.

CLUE: As the characters look from tapestry to tapestry, they see the same figure out of place lurking somewhere in the background. Always staring, always half-human, half something else. In addition, they realise this figure wasn’t in the other tapestries a moment ago. 

C2. Curator Varness’s Quarters

‘Bright Lumens reflect dully off a stained metal desk upon which sits a cogitator, an auto quill, a scattered stack of parchments and a glass tumbler of amasec. Narrow armaglass windows stand in a neat row to its rear, and at the far end of the chamber a bunk lies in disarray near a storage locker.’

Crouched near the pinnacle of the Interminable Devotion are @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness’}s quarters. Unknown to the rest of the crew, a small diary is hidden within a secret compartment of her desk in which she confides her worries and fears over her inadequacy for this post. Linger too long, and the Curator may catch them rifling through her belongings and have to explain themselves.

C3. Captain Viridian’s Quarters

‘Lumens flicker and then grow bright, catching harshly on the many fractured marble tiles and glistening broken glass that floors the small chamber. A desk of dark steel lies upended in the centre of the room while papers lie scattered on the floor around a smashed cogitator. Narrow gothic windows flank one side, overseeing a broken bunk and torn mattress’. 

The party gains the following clue if a character repairs the cogitator with a Challenging (+0) Tech (Engineering) Test or brings it to @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49}. 

CLUE: Much of the data has been corrupted, except for a haunting and distorted vox recording, featuring a recent entry from the captain’s log.

‘I can't… I can't take it anymore… the things, I see them… I hear them and none of the crew can be trusted… There's something going on, someone or something is doing this to all of us… it's in our heads… or is it? I'm not sure which is worse…’ A sudden shout of fury echoes savagely through the recording followed by the sounds of someone breaking and smashing dozens of objects… a few moments of panting follow before the Captain’s voice once more can be heard… ‘It’s up to me… it's all up to me…’

C4. The Bridge 

‘An empty command throne dominates the central space of the large gothic chamber, while rows of deck menials and servitors tap commands onto blinking cogitator screens. Huge armaglass windows reveal an expanse of acidic sludge split harshly by lashing rain in the great glow of the Devotions' powerful lumens before trailing off into an impenetrable dark.’ 

The Devotions' cramped Bridge looms at the front of the Militarum Deck, sitting just below the mighty craft’s formidable battlements. Formerly the foremost seat of power aboard, Captain Veridian gave all orders on navigation and steering, but now the Imperialis’s crew follows commands supplied by Curator Varness. If the characters interview any bridge crew members, they’ll easily sense their paranoia and lack of cohesion among the team; none of them trust each other. If pressed further, succeeding a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Inquiry) Test, the characters learn that most of the bridge crew suspected Captain Viridian of coming apart at the seams, but out here in the wastes, they had no one to turn to.

Time for Communion

Shortly after the party discovers their first clues, they are overcome with a specific vision from being exposed to @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s formula (@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{Chemical Communion}). Get the party to make a Challenging (+0) Fortitude Test, and choose the characters with the least SL to experience the following vision.

‘Passing between decks, you turn onto a lonesome corridor devoid of any crew. Silence reigns in the tight metal space, save for the rhythmic clank of your boot-steps on the rust-patterned floor. Soon, a dreadful dizziness comes over you, the passage groans as if under stress, and its far end seems to distort, almost twisting in place with each step forward. Then you hear it, a dreadful chittering, keening sharp in your ears like coffin nails on slate. It resounds from just inside a nearby chamber.’

Unaffected characters just see the characters stop in place, mumbling gibberish as their hallucination continues.

‘Inside, you see a chamber dimly lit by a single flickering lumen. The floor and walls are spattered in clumps of thick, stinking mud, while sharp, ragged grasses sprout chaotically. Metal and mire meld together in a discordant landscape never meant to be, while at its centre, movement catches your eye. Twisted figures gather around strange ruins at the foot of a large hill, while at their centre a boy kneels in the mud, weeping before a man concealed by the shadows of an alcove.’ 

If a character attempts to shoot or otherwise attack the hallucinations, their blows pass through it as if their target were made of smoke — characters outside the hallucination may have to deal with the character attacking the air in front of them. If the affected characters move further into the chamber, the following occurs.

‘You see a small boy, snivelling before a tall, shrouded figure, he wears the robes of a House Nethecaré Alchemist, the large house crest is unmissable. The shrouded figure steps into the light, his form a horrific amalgamation of acynadi and Human flesh. His stern features are set with spines and mandibles. The boy and the ruins quickly melt away, leaving the man alone in the hill’s shadow. Then the hill begins to move, and you realise it was never a hill. This vast shadow looms over the man as if he is not a man but only the smallest fraction of this gargantuan thing, as if he were only a lure. As the man with the twisted features turns and stares, you feel as if something truly sees you and swiftly the scene melts away, leaving only a bare store room behind.’

The affected character’s consciousness returns to the original corridor, the hallucination passes. Any Damage they might have suffered is removed. If a member of the party is a Psyker, and they make any Test to detect the source of the hallucinations, they find nothing. Only on an Astounding Success (+5 SL or more) do they pick up a faint hint of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji’s }capabilities and the phenomenon in the Hall of Remembrance (that will manifest in @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#new-visions,-old-hatreds]{New Visions, Old Hatreds}). But nothing points to the are of the Capitol Imperialis they’re in.

Price of Succession

As the party discovers more clues to further their investigation, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} continues to pursue his own agenda, rife with complications. 

In the background of the character’s investigation, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos} has been conducting his own, built on a foundation of hunches, but with one significant clue — Drukos believed it was a servitor who killed the Captain, one of Roderick’s medicae servitors, that is currently unaccounted for. This is true, and @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} ordered the servitor to leave the Devotion after the murder, to cover his tracks, while the Imperialis was first halted in the wastes.

Confronting the Medicae alone, the noble tricks @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos}. He knocks the sergeant out, straps him to a medicare bed and injects him with the next version of his concentrated @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. Watching Drukos enraptured by his visions, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} believes he is one step closer to fulfilling his plan. Knowing too much, he kills Drukos in the Medicae Ward while he has the chance. 

Knowing the characters are on his heels, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} decides to swap places with @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos }— abandoning his spider-legged throne, scarring Drukos’s corpse beyond recognition, and retrieving his clothes and vox equipment. He takes to the Devotion’s vents and crawl spaces while he figures out the next stage of his plan, as his delusions continue to aggrandise. 

Eventually, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos’s} body, in the guise of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick}, is discovered. The party hears a horrid scream from the Habitation Deck or a commotion over the Devotion’s security vox channel, drawing them all to the Medicae Ward. 

‘While passing through the Habitation Deck, a scream cuts through the murmur of crew going about their duties. Heads turn at racing bootprints hammering the deck, echoing harshly off metal walls. A medicae adept thunders around a corner, knocking several scribes to the floor in his fervour. His face is pale, his eyes wide, and his mouth agape as he draws deep, laboured breaths. ‘The medicae’, he pants, ‘By the throne, he's dead!’

When the characters reach the Medicae Ward, a throng of onlookers has gathered, though all seem unwilling to enter. Pushing through and stepping inside, the party discovers the following. 

‘Slouched beside a medicae bed, the mechanical legs of Roderick’s support throne lay sprawled with a desecrated corpse heaped upon it. Its face and throat are a ruin of torn flesh, while bloody hands crowned with broken fingernails tell a tale of insanity and horror.’

If the party investigates Roderick’s body, it becomes evident that the Medicae tore himself apart in some sort of apoplectic frenzy. Should the party wish to inspect the body, they are given the following clue. They may also attempt a Challenging (+0) Medicae (Human) Test to acquire an additional clue.

CLUE: Looking at the body, you soon begin to notice oddities. Muscle mass, bone density, and even physical size seem at odds with your expectations. Then it becomes clear: This is not the body of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick. }

CLUE: After completing a more thorough examination, you notice long pressure marks; you deduce this body’s legs and abdomen were strapped down, though no straps are visible now. Furthermore, you discover bruises that suggest something was forcefully injected shortly before death.

Mob Justice

Once the party discovers the previous clues or exhausts their options, their portable vox crackles and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} barks at them — they need to get to the Mess now, as all hell is breaking loose. Upon arriving, read aloud or paraphrase the following: 

‘Ten of Sergeant Drukos’s mercenaries occupy positions beside the long iron counter behind which @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} crouches nervously. At the far end of the Mess, an angry mob of twenty menials led by a large man named @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#menial-boris]{Boris }stands crammed together behind upturned tables, brandishing tools and knives. A length of chain dangles overhead, forming a makeshift noose around a scribe’s neck who stands gagged atop a narrow stool. ‘@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} here is the killer,’ roars Boris ‘Let us give him the Emperor’s justice!’

The menial leader @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#menial-boris]{Boris } appears furious, almost manic, claiming that @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} is the murderer and everyone will be safer once he’s hanged. At the same time, the mercenaries demand their immediate surrender. Boris claims a data slate was slid under the menial Crew Quarters door, holding a report indicating Hess killed Medicae Roderick, along with copies of stock inventories proving he’s been stealing medical supplies. Furthermore, they found stolen pain meds in his robes.

Where’s Drukos?

If the party wonders where Drukos is during this altercation, they may not know yet that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} has killed him. The noble is still imitating him on the Devotion’s security vox channel. He deflects if anyone asks where he is, saying he is busy. Secretly, Vesterick Nethecaré is hoping the mob kills Scribe Hess, playing into the dataslate evidence he planted to incriminate the scribe. But acting as @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos}, he must hold back from directly implicating the scribe without being present.

The party needs to act within a window of five rounds to save the scribe. They must make a Challenging (+0) Extended Rapport (Charm or Deception) Test requiring a total of 6 SL to defuse the situation. If they fail, the scribe’s stool is kicked, and battle erupts between the mob and the mercenaries. It takes @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} three rounds to die. After this outcome, the party may obtain Hess’s note from his body (see the following clues).

However, if the party defuses the situation, the mob will disperse, Scribe Hess is saved, and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}’s men will arrest @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#menial-boris]{Boris}. 

After this outcome, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} approaches the party, thanking them for their help. He explains that he did steal medical supplies but did not commit the murders, revealing his habit of flagellating himself in devotion to the God-Emperor. With the completion of this scene, Scribe Hess can provide the party with the following either by himself or via his notes.

CLUE: ‘I’ve noted strange mechanical errors in the Devotions air filtration system. I think one of the menials needs to be assigned to go down to the Enginarium Deck and check the filters.’

If Hess survives, the party can be supplied with an additional clue. 

CLUE: ‘I reported these errors to @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} a few days ago while she was meeting with @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick}. The Medicae said he would arrange @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49} to sort it out, and told me not to worry about it.’

If the party approaches @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49}, questioning him regarding this task, he claims not to have received the request. Should the party go to the Enginarium Deck to investigate the air filters, provide them with the following clue.

CLUE: ‘A dark waxy substance coats the filters in a film of sticky residue. Much has built up in the moving parts gumming the mechanism, which undoubtedly caused the errors Hess detected. From this buildup, it is clear some strange contaminant is present in the Devotion's air supply.’

New Visions, Old Hatreds

After the former ordeal, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} soon approaches the party. He seems off, fearful even, like a man on the edge. 

‘Old Hinji can hear him, but even if I couldn't, I'd know anyway, it ain't right, he ain’t right. You better come with me, I gots something to tell you that's not for others listening.’

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji }then leads them to the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#c1.-the-hall-of-remembrance]{Hall of Remembrance} on the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#c.-militarum-deck]{Militarum Deck}. Reaching the door, his breath fogs as the air turns cold, the metal door handle clinging to their fingers. Once inside, Old Hinji provides the party with the following.

‘He won’t follow us here. I know that much at least. I think he hates this place as much as I do. It's Drukos, he's not himself anymore. I'm not sure what's happened, but it's dark business. Drukos was my friend, and that man on the vox isn’t him; he’s been someone else, or someone else is being him. Ugh... I can feel him, his mind, I think, memories skittering around on too many legs.’

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} collapses and begins convulsing violently.

‘The temperature suddenly plummets as the figures within the central tapestry begin to move. Acynadi appear to escape the tapestry, all shapes and sizes spilling out into the Hall of Remembrance, transforming and shifting into ever-increasing different configurations.’

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, brought to life by Hinji’s unwilling projection of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s memories and his growing paranoia, begin to attack the characters. Tentacles and claws grow across the floor and walls, making the Hall Difficult Terrain and two @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5} spill out of the tapestries and begin to attack the party. If one is slain, another spawns to replace it at the start of the following round.

As each round begins the tapestry shifts, forming a memory Old Hinji has unwillingly projected. 

1: ‘You see a noble youth, fearful among tall spires. Weeping for his lost father, his kin laugh as his mother remarries a smirking old scion, in his heart, he knows they killed him.’

2: ‘The youth is older now. Toiling over intricate experiments, he searches, questing and failing. Frustrated, he fills a syringe with one of his concoctions, injects himself and dreams.’

3: ‘Inside the dream, his father is waiting with the formula and the plan. He has communed with the dead! He is sure of it, more sure than anything. But the formula isn’t perfect, it is his purpose to complete it.’

A psyker character may attempt a Hard (−20) Psychic Mastery (Telepathy) Test in order to calm the psychic projections for a round. After three rounds are complete, the tapestries flutter and return to normal. Old Hinji rises, panting, sweating and weak. The characters recover any Damage the projections did to them.

‘Get him for me will ya, for all of us. That bastard killed my friend and I'd wager he's fixing to kill the rest of us too. He's utterly insane, but I think whatever he’s been taking has only gotten worse.’ 

If the party asks what happened, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} replies that he's not sure; he felt the false Drukos’s memories calling to him, but he doesn't understand. He swiftly leaves, eager for rest. If the characters figure out now that he is a rogue psyker, they may wish to lock him up before he manifests any more warp phenomena.

pages.name: Part 3: A Mind in Ruins
pages.text:
At this point, the party should have enough information to suspect that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} is behind the murders and is currently posing as @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}. If not, use the following events to bring the investigation forward:

  • If they decide to search the Interminable Devotion for @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Drukos}, who keeps dodging their presence, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} can slip up in his imitations of the sergeant over the vox by giving incorrect details or acting rashly. If you need to press the point, members of Drukos’ squad could approach the Party asking if they’ve seen him.

  • If @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} is still alive, they’ll have inspected the Medicae’s (Drukos’) body and concluded that the corpse is @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}, adding that the Medicae has been missing all day.

  • If none of the above works, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} calls the party to her cabin for a progress report, after which you can begin the following scenes.

The party must present their findings to @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness}. She thinks the idea of a hidden Nethecaré noble being responsible is initially preposterous. Unbeknownst to the party, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} is listening in through the small vox receiver he hid in her augmentic hand some time ago under the guise of @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick}.

The party meeting with @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Varness} triggers the climax of the adventure. Once finished stating their case, but before the party leaves the Curator’s cabin, the chamber is swallowed in darkness before red emergency lights kick in. Then the craft-wide vox crackles, and the following can be heard.

‘My my, aren’t you the clever little lab rats? Unfortunately for you, you still find yourselves within my maze and I can’t have you scuttling off and spoiling things, there are grander things at work here.’ 

Then the groaning sound of aching metal splits the air as the Devotion rocks sharply. Each character must make a Challenging (+0) Athletics (Climbing) Test or be knocked Prone and suffer 3 Damage. The vox then crackles again, the voice now frantic, rapturous even. 

‘He’s come… he’s finally come for me… he’s come to save me… father, I’m here!... Let this be my parting gift to you. The formula works! Breathe in the blessing of chemical communion!’  

A hiss sounds as a pungent, sickly sweet odour fills the air. The characters must make a Hard (−20) Fortitude (Poison) Test as @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} releases his communion at full concentration aboard the Devotion (see @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#contamination]{Contamination}). 

‘Curator Varness races to her cogitator, typing frantically. ‘Something has crippled the Devotion’s left track. We’re paralysed,’ she coughs. ‘And that bastard might have sealed us in, but if we can get down to the Hangar, we should be able to release that door manually.’  

Vesterick's Plotting

As the characters cobble together their last clues and present their findings to @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness}, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} has put his final plans into motion. Hiding between the Devotion’s decks and crawlspaces, he has created the final form of his chemical communion and has set it up to distribute throughout the Capitol Imperialis’s air filtration system.

At the same time, the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }outside the Devotion have continued to swarm towards it. All this time, some of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s chemical communion has been leaking from the Capitol Imperialis, the pheromone component within the formula has been attracting the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}. A behemoth-sized, latently psychic, and unclassified acynadi is about to strike the Interminable Devotion. 

When @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} sees this colossal @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi} coming, he believes his father has come back for him, and seeks to escape the Imperialis and meet him in the nearby ruins.

Rush to Save the Crew

The party is challenged to descend through the Devotion’s decks as chemical-induced madness overtakes the crew. Their goal is to reach the Hangar and vent the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} from the Devotion’s decks (if they do not think of this solution, Varness can pose it to them). If they have a workable solution of their own design, use the following encounters to hamper their movement towards their goal.

In each challenge, failure causes the character to make another Hard (−20) Fortitude (Poison) Test to resist the@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{ chemical communion}.

‘Beyond the Curators’ cabin, the sound of maddened screams and gunfire fills the Militarum Deck as manic mercenaries fire at one another and things only they seem to see.’ 

In this first challenge, the characters need to avoid or confront the mercenaries. They could make a Challenging (+0) Reflexes (Dodge) or Stealth (Move Silently) Test to avoid them, or find a different route with a Challenging (+0) Navigation (Tracking) or Tech (Engineering) to find an alternate route. Treat the corridors as a Minor Hazard if the characters fail their Tests.

‘Passing down a stairwell, another shudder rocks the Devotion as something batters it from outside threatening to send you all tumbling down the narrow metal stairs.’ 

In this second challenge, the characters need to pass a Hard (−20) Athletics (Climbing) or Fortitude (Endurance) Test to stay on their feet. If they fail they fall Prone and take Damage equal to their negative SL.

‘Entering the Habitation Deck you see huge gangs of menials running through the passages, jagged metal and tools in their blood slick hands. Howling like beasts they drag a screaming scribe out from under a bunk and bludgeon him to death.’ 

In this third challenge, the characters can choose to aid the captured scribe, or continue on to keep pace. If they choose to aid the scribe, they’ll fall behind and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} will get to the Hangar release before them (described at the end of these encounters), and they’ll be forced to make another Hard (−20) Fortitude (Poison) Test to resist the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} for lingering. Otherwise ask them to make a Test similar to the first challenge to avoid the mob, but the area is considered a Major Hazard if they fail.

‘Reaching the Enginarium Deck you see menials and haywire servitors thrashing about, under the effects of the chemical communion. Some are crowding near the hangar door’s control console, and they notice you.’ 

In this fourth challenge, the characters are confronted by two menials (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourer} stat-block to represent them) and two @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.px7pplClKR01chqM]{Servitor}. Under the effects of the chemical communion, they attack randomly, perhaps even each other, and all Tests against them are at Advantage. The characters are four Zones away from the door controls, located up a small gantry way next to the door aperture. They can avoid the assailants and reach the hangar’s door control console by making a Difficult (−10) Athletics (Climbing) or Reflexes (Dodge) Test instead, but failing causes them to fall into the fight.

No test is needed to activate the door’s release mechanism, so long as someone reaches it and hits the clearly marked button, then proceed to the next section.

Old Hinji’s Fate

If the characters do not make it there in time, or all succumb to the effects of the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji} comes to the crew’s rescue in their stead. He senses his way to the Hangar and releases the hangar door, allowing the toxic gas to drain from the Devotion’s decks.

The party finds him next to the hangar door console on the brink of death, having been pushed to his limit. Only a Very Hard (−30) Medicae (Human) Test can stabilise him, otherwise he’ll promptly die after relaying the following information.

If the characters made it to the hangar door console in time, they’ll find Old Hinji nearby; exhausted. He’ll need medicae attention, but no Test is required to stabilise him.

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji }tells the party he ran into @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick} (@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}) on his way to the Hangar, and has some vital information for them: 

‘Ruins outside, he said he was going to meet his father in the ruins’.
