The chemical communion vents out of the Interminable Devotion, but at the same time, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }of various sizes begin to enter the Hangar from outside, investigating the source of the airborne pheramones (mostly tiny variants and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.7F9x6CZCJCp0IV6b]{Acynadi Beta-3}, among a few more ornery @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}). The characters can aid in setting up barricades and warding the enemy tide off, or you can skip to the next section; some of the Devotion’s security and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49}’s servitors come to do the job regardless.

Stalled in the Wastes

Regrouping with @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varnes}s, she speculates how @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} could have known they were on to him. If the characters do not search her office or augmetic arm for the hidden vox caster, Varness discovers it alone. She curses herself as a fool and destroys the device. 

She relays the state of the Devotion to the characters. Whatever hit the Capitol Imperialis caused the ancient engine to stall, and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49} is working to get it moving again. They won’t be underway for some time. Regardless, the crew is in shambles. Their minds are broken, and many of them are dead. Anyone still alive is fending off the stray @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }who scuttled aboard or is patching up the engine.

To gain some form of victory from this ordeal, the Curator presses the party to finish their job and chase down @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} once and for all. She hands them a report formed from the Devotion’s augur scans, and only one patch of ruins is nearby, marked on an attached map. They have a moment to catch their breath but must make haste to find the madman.

The Ruins

Leaving the Devotion and emerging into the storm-wracked acidic wilderness, the party’s portable lumens soon reveal dozens of huge depressions scattered around the side of the Capitol Imperialis. These are immense footprints, each at least twenty feet wide, leading out into the dark. Armed with a data slate loaded with geographic reconnaissance data, the party knows the ruins aren’t far. 

The area is filled with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi}, though they are more interested in getting into the Devotion than getting in the character’s way. They reach the edge of the ruins unhampered, read or paraphrase the following:

‘Sharp lines of acidic rain cut through the bright beams of your portable lumens as you see them, rotten and fang-like. Ragged stone structures, broken and ruined, leer out of the storm forming angular walls, crumbled pillars and sharp-edged obelisks.’ 

They should easily notice that no @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }are in the ruins, as if they won’t step inside. The few they see seem to stand still at the edge. As they move deeper, the outcrops of stones grow closer together until something resembling a massive ruined structure looms out of the dark, its huge circular entryway yawning like a vast, hungry maw. Read or paraphrase the following:

‘The winding passages terminate in a huge circular chamber, its domed ceiling, cracked and broken, looms precariously as the storm winds whip through in a series of keening howls. Huge, crumbling pillars dominate the space in a forest of shattered stone while at the centre a raised dias supports an altar inlaid with strange spirals.’

Investigating the Ruins

The characters should be making haste to confront @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}, but if any of them halt to glance at the ruins, you can reveal some of the following information.

  • Apart from the crumbling parts of the structure, none of the ruins’s architecture present seams or breaks between the stonework, seeming impossible to construct by conventional imperial means.

  • The only markings on the ruins surfaces (walls and floors) are strange, spiral-like indentations; some are small, thumb-sized spirals, others take up entire spans of rock.

  • The stone appears incredibly acid-resistant. Unlike imperial construction, there are no acid-markings from centuries of being submerged in Voll’s acidic swampland.

Once inside the inner chamber, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} makes his presence known, stepping onto the raised dais at the chamber's centre. He insults the party, mocking them for their stupidity as he hid right under their noses. As his madness and paranoia come to the fore, read aloud or paraphrase the following:

‘They sent you to ruin this for me, didn't they? Didn't they?! Who was it? My Uncle? One of his heirs? They’ve always tried to keep me down, pushing my nose into the dirt so they can laugh like I wasn't a Nethecaré! But not anymore! I’ve solved the formula! The chemical communion! My formula will bring the house to new heights!’ Behind him, heavy, thunderous, plodding steps approach the ruins, shaking the earth and threatening everyone to their knees. Vesterick cackles madly, withdrawing an odd-looking grenade. ‘You see! Father is coming, father is coming to rescue me!’ He pulls the pin on the grenade, dropping it at his feet. It releases a thick plume of orange gas as he vanishes into the forest of pillars.’

Once among the pillars, characters can attempt to make a Challenging (+0) Perception (Sight) Test to search for @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}. Should they be successful, they hear the unmistakable click of a pin being pulled from a grenade before a sudden plume of bright orange gas erupts around them. Characters must make a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Poison) Test to resist the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. Any character who was successful in their Perception Test may make the Fortitude Test with Advantage as they anticipate the coming hazard. 

@UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} aims to attack those he’s afflicted with his chemical communion, evading the party until he can get the drop on them. Three rounds after combat begins, as the heavy footsteps grow closer, the following occurs:

‘The colossal thumping footsteps now hammer the ground beyond the chamber’s walls, each thunderous boom louder than the storm as the ground trembles. Something huge beyond reckoning and dark as the night smashes a section of the domed ceiling, sending large chunks of stone plummeting to the floor.’

The party must make a Challenging (+0) Reflexes (Dodge) Test to avoid the falling stone. On a failure, they are knocked Prone and suffer 5 Damage. All Zones gain the Lightly Obscured Environmental Trait from all the silt and debris kicked up into the air. Meanwhile, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} continues to evade the party as best he can in the same manner as before. Debris continues to fall into different Zones for another two rounds, then the following occurs: 

‘A horrible scream cuts through the din, and you see Vesterick Nethecaré, his legs pinned beneath a heavy piece of rubble. ‘Father,’ he screams. ‘Father, please help me!’ As if beckoned by his call, a huge tentacular claw emerges from the shadowed canopy beyond the dome. Slimy, glistening and dotted with small bioluminescent pits so synonymous with deep water acynadi. It reaches towards him.’

The party can react in a number of ways, but make it clear to them that they only have six rounds to escape the ruins unscathed:

They may wish to free @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} from the rubble and take him back to the Interminable Devotion, to answer for his crimes and face the God-Emperor’s justice. Freeing him requires an extended Hard (+20) Athletics (Might) Group Test, requiring 8 total SL to succeed. The party has three rounds in which to succeed in freeing Vesterick Nethecaré before the giant creature seizes him and draws him out into the blackness beyond the ruins.

However, the party may wish to escape right away, as it should be clear that the ceiling has become critically unstable. Fleeing the ruins requires a Routine (−20) Reflexes (Dodge) or Athletics (Running) Test as they move around the falling debris. They need to succeed at this Test twice to escape individually. If they are dragging @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} along, the Difficulty of these Tests increases to Hard (+20). Failing this Test, a chunk of debris hits them for 3 Damage, or on a Critical Failure, they are also knocked Prone.

If the party takes any opportunity to go through @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s possessions, they find a dataslate detailing the formula for his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} along with three of his remaining gas grenades.

As the party emerges into the wilderness, the ruined structure behind them crumbles as they narrowly avoid its total collapse. As the dust cloud subsides, they notice all the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }that had gathered are now gone. Furthermore to their relief the storm seems to be moving off and the sky begins to brighten. Read aloud or paraphrase the following:

‘The raging storm seems to shift to the west away from the Interminable Devotion and deeper into the barren acidic wasteland. The darkness within the lashing tempest seems to swallow the oncoming landscape under the shrouding pressure of its heavy clouds. Yet every so often a flash of lightning illuminates that dark inner world and in its after image you see a shape, vast and monolithic, moving in its blackened depths.’

With the storm moving the characters see salvation nearby in the proud defiant shape of the Interminable Devotion, its armored battlements dominating the landscape, beckoning them to return to safety.

pages.name: Aftermath
pages.text:
With @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} defeated or lost, his plan foiled, and the formula for his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} recovered or destroyed, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} and the reputation of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#nethecare]{House Nerthecaré} have been spared horrific damage. The party can return to the Interminable Devotion and contact their Patron for extraction. @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness}, if she is in good standing with the party, will back their version of events and thank the party for thwarting Vesterick Nethecaré’s plan.

The characters make arrangements to recover the Capitol Imperialis if their Patron tasked them to do so. However, if they do not, @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#mathus-49]{Mathus-49} contacts his superiors, and the craft is eventually recovered by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} before undergoing a significant retrofit for future deployment. Some NPCs the characters encountered could become Contacts or available as hirelings in their future adventures, such as @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Curator Varness} and @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji}.

Experience Points

All characters should earn @Reward[xp=30 reason=Interminable Devotion]{30 XP} for participating in the adventure. If any characters achieved personal goals or fulfilled a goal for their Patron, their reward should be increased accordingly. In addition, the following experience can be awarded:

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Reached the Interminable Devotion]{10 XP} for reaching the Interminable Devotion in Part 1.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason= Saved Scribe Hess]{10 XP} for saving @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#scribe-hess]{Scribe Hess} in Part 2.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Vented the chemical communion]{10 XP} for venting the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion} in Part 3.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Figured out Medicae Roderick's true identity]{10 XP} for figuring out @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#medicae-roderick]{Medicae Roderick}’s true identity.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Confronted Vesterick Nethecaré]{20 XP} for confronting @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} in the ruins.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Acquired or destroyed Vesterick Nethecaré formula]{20 XP} for acquiring or destroying @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s formula.

Influence

Award or reduce the character's Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily House Nethecaré as a result of sparing their reputation from their misbegotten sons' planned sabotage. Additionally, increase or reduce each character’s Personal Influence according to their behaviour and decisions surrounding the fate of NPCs who related to the wider factions at work throughout the Macharian Sector. These factions include the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists} (Trackless Chain). As a result these effects may in turn influence their Patron’s influences depending on their behavior. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

Should the party fail to capture or eliminate @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} before the massive creature he refers to as his ‘father’ can seize him, they must retreat from the crumbling ruins empty-handed. Leaving the rubble behind and despite seeing their adversary carried off by some gargantuan creature, the party won’t be able to shake the feeling that the noble is still out there.

@UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#old-hinji]{Old Hinji }reinforces this feeling, if he is still alive at this point in the adventure, who speaks it aloud to the party. Without Vesterick Nethecaré or the formula for his chemical communion, the party must trek back to the Devotion with a strange disquiet heavy in their guts.

Otherwise, there may be a chance that @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} is somewhat successful and escaped with his formula. The next time the party encounters the noble, it may be to thwart his plans to infect @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-dalal]{Hive Dalal} with his @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, turning the populace mad and drawing a massive population of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }to attack the hive.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • The Interminable Devotion sits in ruins from the chaos that so recently wracked its decks. One of its vast tracks sprawls in broken disorder, while inside its mechanical guts, cables, relays and piping are laid bare. While the great engine has suffered extreme damage, it is not beyond repair. It would take a dedicated team and considerable resources to revive this iron leviathan — the race is on between the scavengers gangs, @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#nethecare]{House Nethecaré} and the local @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}.

  • A whisper can be just as potent as any toxic chemical with a half-life powerful and persistent enough to cause a fallout. Upon returning to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, some of the Devotion’s survivors have been less than tight-lipped about what happened. Most were unaware of any noble involvement, but rumours of strange @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }behaviour were rampant. Word has spread of a chemical that draws the typically skittish and hard-to-hunt acynadi together in large numbers. As a result, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-stilt-fleet]{Stilt-fleets} and acynadi hunting teams are already searching for it. Such an agent would be worth a fortune to the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#carnem]{Mercador Carnem}, but in the wrong hands could spell disaster.

pages.name: Dramatis Personae
pages.text:
The Interminable Devotion shelters some two hundred souls from the storm-wracked darkness beyond its walls. Some are major players who influence the ebb and flow of power upon the craft, while others fade into the faceless morass of downtrodden souls. Each major character holds information that can inform the party of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s presence and agenda. 

Apart from these characters, the Interminable Devotion is crewed by a mix of menials (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers}), @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.px7pplClKR01chqM]{Servitors}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adepts}, and @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Troopers}.

Curator Varness

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.Dhe0z7z8c9ZFDeM0 description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Curator Varness}

Roleplaying the Curator 

As this is her first senior post, the Curator is eager to do well and to put forward an air of authority and unflappable leadership. However, she fears that she is far out of her depth. Initially, she is curt and to the point, providing only the information the party needs and supplying what is requested in as few words as possible. As the adventure moves on and pressure builds, the cracks in her mask begin to show. She becomes prone to barking orders and stumbling over her words.

The Curator takes to plying herself with amasec, resulting in an acrid smell that follows her like a cloud. She harbours an incredible fear of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}, heightened due to the effects of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}’s @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}. If the party’s Patron is an Inquisitor, and Varness becomes aware of this fact, she aims to avoid speaking to the party, making it evident that she is hiding something. If pressed, she swiftly cracks and provides the clue below.

CLUE: Fearful of the Inquisition’s intervention, Varness destroyed almost all reports of strange phenomena recorded by the Devotion’s expedition and reported by the crew. The Curator then divulges that she formally held a low-ranking position and was given this assignment and rank by a mysterious benefactor. All paperwork was marked with a wax seal bearing the initials ‘V.N.’ (unaware it was Vesterick Nethecaré).

Mathus-49

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Curator Varness}

Medicae Roderick

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ncXwqNsh38L8CyRo description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Medicae Roderick}

Roleplaying Medicae Roderick

When roleplaying Medicae Roderick, you are roleplaying a disguise of @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré}. He has become a talented mimic and has had long years to perfect his guise as the kindly old Medicae, he can still occasionally slip into older, more typically highborn speech patterns. Medicae Roderick is helpful and understanding, eager to assist when troubles or ailments might be eased. As a result, he is a well-liked figure amongst the Devotion’s crew with a reputation for wisdom and warmth. Should he be questioned about advising @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#curator-varness]{Varness} to destroy reports, he states truthfully that he felt it was in the expedition’s best interests. 

As the story progresses, @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#vesterick-nethecare]{Vesterick Nethecaré} usurps @UUID[.u9wPwSqM2FTyo8pg#sergeant-drukos]{Sergeant Drukos}’s identity to cover his tracks. Think of this as another mask behind which the same character you have been portraying already hides. You may even drop subtle hints after this event occurs, such as Drukos’s renowned grim demeanour being broken by the odd jovial remark or helpful offer as Vesterick Nethecaré struggles to break the habits of his former guise.

CLUE: Should the players wish to cast a critical eye over Roderick, they may make a Routine (+20) Intuition (People) Test. Upon success, they realise that on occasion, how the Medicae orders his words is somewhat elaborate, extravagant even, almost as if he were of noble birth.

Menial Boris

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.XfuOWlQ5fvUgtElU description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Menial Boris}

Old Hinji

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Old Hinji}

Roleplaying Old Hinji

Despite his impairments, Old Hinji is a jovial and animated fellow fond of chatter and eager to find ears to listen to him. He happily wiles away the hours discussing almost anything with anyone, especially when a strong drink is offered. He is also an infamous gambler, the only crewman to have never lost a game of ‘Dagger Counts’ in @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b2.-the-mess]{the Mess}.

Most write off the old man’s attachment to @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#b2.-the-mess]{the Mess} to his love of drinking and gambling; however, Old Hinji sticks close to the Mess because he fears being alone. Though unaware of his psychic potential, due to the effects of the @UUID[.3BlX4i31o2Wez7vh#chemical-communion]{chemical communion}, he believes that a strange @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }presence is calling out to him. Immersing himself in the chatter of the Mess drones out the worst of it. Yet many of these delusions persist and spinning them into tales is the only way he can manage to cope.

Spending any significant time with Old Hinji, he tells the characters the following tale. 

CLUE: ‘There was a boy once… a boy that lived in high towers, sharp as knives and tall as the clouds. Yet the folk he lived with were sharper still, and they did away with this father and married his mother off to some lord or other… t’was his kin that did it… Wretched doings, and the boy never got over it. He spoke to the shadows that come about when you’re at that sort of business… but he never could feel any better, I think his mind ‘as gone a bit rotten now… poor lad… I just hope he doesn’t hurt anyone.’

Scribe Hess

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Scribe Hess}

Sergeant Drukos

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.wyyOOGQNpAYh5Txm description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]{Sergeant Drukos}

Roleplaying Sergeant Drukos

Having secured such a lucrative contract for him and his men in an out-of-the-way place with so little risk feels almost too good to be true. As a result, Drukos takes his position as sergeant quite seriously, eager to get this mission done, enjoy his earnings and secure potential future employment. 

Yet all of this fine luck is not enough to lift his spirits. The threat of his past lingers like a ghost in the back of his mind. He’s paranoid that one day he will be discovered by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} for desertion. then it will be his skull getting the last las-round. Drukos will not easily give up the information about his shady past unless persuaded with a Hard (−20) Rapport (Charm) Test or confronted with hard evidence. The characters can find this evidence if they notice the inconsistencies found in the personnel files in the @UUID[.vC2n6yi7x19C9HvR#a2.-central-cogitarum]{Cogitarum}, granting the following clue.

CLUE: Drukos and his mercenaries are deserters of the Astra Militarum. Having only secured this contract by the aid of a mysterious benefactor who provided falsified papers and identity tags. These documents were marked with a wax seal bearing the initials V.N. (once more standing for Vesterick Nethecaré).

pages.name: Paradigm Shift
pages.text: Paradigm Shift takes players from the decadent hab of a minor noble in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} through a decrepit hab sprawl and down into the corrupted bowels of a toxic refinery. Perils lurking in the dark will test the character’s resistance to corruption, courage in the face of Chaos, and dedication to the sacred duty they owe the God-Emperor. Paradigm Shift can serve as a stand-alone experience played over 2–3 sessions or, should they survive, as part of a more extensive campaign.

pages.name: Adventure Overview
pages.text:
Paradigm Shift is a three-part adventure, with the bulk of the action taking place in and underneath Maltus Refinery VI in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Lower Hive area. While brute force and violence have their uses, investigation, exploration, and secrecy are the weapons most valuable here.

@UUID[.eIrwUyweHDHkZGjP]{Part 1: Initial Investigations} — The characters begin the adventure by meeting the noble-in-distress, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, whose wealth, life, and social position are at risk due to mysterious problems at his refinery. He lends them his bodyguard, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik}, to aid their investigation. They can question the Lord’s household, the refinery’s former workers, and the Magos who conducted the last inspection.

@UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8]{Part 2: The Refinery} — The characters dive into the depths of Maltus Refinery VI. Dealing with scalding vapours streaming from damaged conduits and acid overflowing from bursting pipes makes their traversal challenging. Clues they find along the way can lead the characters to encounter the bestial Abhumans who have been forced to work here. These @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have killed their overseers and captured their former leader, devoting themselves to Chaos. Cut off from the outside world, the characters need to find another way to escape the manufactorum. 

@UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY]{Part 3: The Tunnels} — The party must traverse the lower pipeways beneath the manufactorum, where the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Beastmen’s Shaman} has worked his terrible psychic powers. To find the exit, they must pass through the Shaman’s lair and face the corrupt leader of the Beastmen himself.

@UUID[.RcIUQQRgCBlLd63s]{Aftermath} — The adventure concludes with the characters confronting @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, who seeks to purge the refinery and surrounding habsprawls without admitting the presence of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}. The noble offers them a lucrative deal; will they side with the corrupt noble, or risk going against him?

Maltus Refinery VI

Manufactorum Maltus Refinery VI is a sprawling mass of pipes, vats, boilers, and pumping stations that refines the toxic muck of Voll into… well, no one is quite sure. The Administratum’s voluminous records note a daily expected output of thousands of sealed barrels from the refinery, simply labelled ‘Chemical VOL-48S’. By ancient writ, these barrels are distributed to other manufactorums on Voll, and a handful are shipped off-world. Here, they no doubt serve some arcane purpose, but no outsider has set foot in Maltus Refinery VI in at least two centuries, and no one has any idea what that might be. The workers toil in ignorance of what purpose their suffering might serve, but toil they must, for the refinery’s output is a small part of Voll’s tithe to the Imperium. It is one of a dozen holdings of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, a minor figure in his house but one whose modest standing is nevertheless dependent on the refinery’s output.

Some time ago, this output began to drop. Familiar with the workshy habits of malingering labourers, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} ordered an increase in disciplinary measures. It quickly became clear, however, that ordinary measures would be insufficient. No amount of morale measures seemed to help, and an inspection by an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} Magos finally revealed why. The centuries had taken their toll on the facility, and while its core mechanisms continued to function, the Magos explained, the facility’s machine spirits had grown moribund and discontent. The result was the discharge of several harmful compounds onto the work floor and a commensurate spike in illness, injury, and death among the workers.

The Magos further explained to an increasingly distraught @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} that repair of the facility would be a low priority as the damage was non-critical. Such ‘low priority’ repairs could take decades to arrange, and so other plans were made. New workers were requisitioned, but all quickly succumbed to the facility’s toxic conditions. Eventually, Lord Felputh could no longer make excuses for his diminishing contributions toward the planetary tithe. He would increase his output and compensate for the shortfall, or be replaced by someone else who could. In utter desperation, Lord Felputh searched for a solution to allow him to retain his position.

Lord Felputh’s Folly

Eventually, a contact from the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW#rogue-traders-of-note]{Klaskoloff Rogue Trader Dynasty} came to him with a solution so unexpected that the nobleman nearly rejected it outright. They proposed supplying a workforce who could survive in the refinery, but whose very nature would offend his neighbours, staff, even the common labourers they replaced. Nevertheless, desperate times called for desperate measures, and desperation was the only thing Lord Felputh had left in abundance.

Not long after, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} received the first consignment of these new hardier labourers. Smuggled in under the cover of a supposed pipeline leak, a few cowering workers nevertheless spied the braying figures led through the near-abandoned habways — @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}.

At first, everything seemed to go as planned. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}, as promised, were far more robust than ordinary Imperial citizens and seemed entirely untroubled by the toxic fumes that had felled shift after shift before them. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s next contribution to the tithe was as it should have been, and if he pushed his new workers just a little harder, he would soon make up his deficit. It seemed he had found the solution to his problem and, as long as he maintained secrecy, all would be well.

After reports of disappearances began circulating in the surrounding hab-blocks, then a noticeable breakdown of communications and access at the refinery, production was forced to halt entirely and the refinery gates were barred shut. Now Lord Felputh is at his wits’ end and finally willing to seek outside help. Of course, it is essential that if, as he fears, the Beastmen are to blame, their presence in the refinery is never traced back to him.

Beastmen!

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} are Abhumans with bestial traits, often including features difficult to conceal, such as horns, tusks, and cloven hooves. While greatly varied in appearance and demeanour, they tend to be robust, fast, and agile. Tougher than most Humans, they can survive in environments Humans cannot.

Beastmen are severely persecuted throughout the Imperium. On many worlds, they are hunted down and slaughtered as unclean mutants. In the rare regions where their existence is tolerated, Beastmen are indoctrinated into self-loathing. They are told to atone for their miscreation through unquestioning service to the God-Emperor and Humanity. Treated little better than Servitors or beasts of burden, Beastmen are put to work in the most dangerous environments. When called to battle, they are armed with simple weapons and herded into war zones as shock troops or cannon fodder.

Despite their feral appearance, Beastmen are quite Human in their reasoning and intelligence, and a great many understand all too well the injustices they must endure. It is little wonder that many Beastmen succumb to the lure of Chaos, embracing their mutations as gifts from the Dark Gods and turning their savagery upon their pitiless Imperial taskmasters.

pages.name: Part 1: Initial Investigations
pages.text:
@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s compound is among the Hive Spires, in the exclusive, well-defended upper-class echelons of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. If the characters haven’t been to the Hive Spires before, they travel by maglift from the upper hive, and their entry should be challenged by a pair of @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilites}. The papers they carry are genuine, but unless the characters appear to belong in the Hive Spires, the Vigilites may require some persuasion (or a bribe) to let them through unhindered.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s address, in the Steeple district, is on the papers. Two of his household guards are stationed at the entrance. They are ex-militarum and can be represented by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Trooper}, though they carry no grenades, and their armour is a bright magenta. The characters must convince the guards they have an appointment; they’re viewed with suspicion despite their proper papers. In any case, before being admitted to the atrium, they are instructed to remove their weapons as well as their acid-stained outer garments and footwear.

Beyond the atrium, a vast echoing hall awaits. A shrine to the God-Emperor looms over the characters from the far end, and doors on either side lead into the rest of the building. Unless the characters try the doors, they won’t realise they are false. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felput}h had to sell much of his ancestral compound to pay debts and maintain his staff, so he’s gone to great pains to ensure his home still appears far larger than it is.

Here they are met by a black-clad woman, decked with knives and twin autopistols hanging unobstructed from her belt. This is @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik}. She ignores any questions and leads them through one of the many doors, into a small chamber. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} is waiting here, sitting on a throne-like chair behind an armaglass screen (the screen provides him with an additional 5 Armour).

Interviewing Lord Felputh

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} takes the characters’ papers and presents them to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, slipping them through a box in the protective screen. The noble scrutinises them before welcoming the characters and thanking them for coming to his aid. He plays the part of a concerned ruler deeply troubled by what might have happened at the plant. He claims his problems are caused by a worker uprising, though if pressed, he admits that the speed at which it happened and the lack of any demands make this seem somewhat unlikely. He mentions that @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Brandt Kesker} was stirring up so much trouble among the former workers that Felputh was forced to replace them all.

If the players ask more about @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker}, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} tells them the labourer is likely living in the habsprawl near the refinery, since he graciously allowed the workers to continue living there despite being unable to employ them any longer. If the players ask why the workers caused trouble or why he could no longer use them, Felputh admits there was some trouble with conditions at the plant, but the Magos who inspected it assured him that no urgent repairs were necessary. If questioned further, Felputh supplies the name of the Magos, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Elipses Vark}, who now works in Forge-Fane Incalcos-6 (located among @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Hive Spires).

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} is grateful to the characters for looking into his problem and insists they take @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} with them as a guide and protector (if they manage to refuse, Sandik follows them from a stealthy distance). He asks that they don’t linger in his home, however, as the presence of such ‘visitors’ might invite suspicion.

While Felputh is keen for the characters to leave, they might wish to question his household guards on the way out. They initially seem reluctant to talk, but if the characters speak to one out of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik}’s hearing, the guard reveals what they know: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} has been docking their pay for the most minor of infringements recently, and the guards are concerned that his wealth, and therefore their livelihood, are at risk. Always a paranoid employer, the noble has been especially fearful of late, and his moods have become more erratic. The trouble with the refinery has made him desperate, and possibly dangerous.

Interviewing Magos Elipses Vark

The characters may wish to seek out @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Magos Elipses Vark} at Forge-Fane Incalcos-6. If they ask for Vark directly, they are told to wait outside, as the Tech-Priests have no intention of admitting outsiders to the Forge-Fane. After an hour of waiting, the Magos, along with a pair of armed servitors, meets with the party just beyond the gates, that seal shut abruptly behind him. He only has time to answer a few questions before excusing himself to return to his work.

Forge-Fane Incalcos-6 is detailed in @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf]{Rokarth: A Guide to the Hive}. It is the sanctum mechanicum of the Cult of Mars in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, where the highest-ranking Tech-Priests in Rokarth pursue their essential and esoteric works. It is a veritable fort of knowledge; even Tech-Priests and Tech-adepts within the Adeptus Mechanicus have trouble accessing the building.

From Vark, the characters can learn about his inspection of the refinery. No urgent repairs were required, but plenty of minor ones could have been hurried along if @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} had been willing to make an appropriate donation to the Tech-Priesthood of Mars. Vark expresses concern that Felputh was more concerned with fulfilling the tithe than appeasing the machine-spirits. He believes the conditions of the refinery must be so poor by now that no Humans could possibly work there safely. Vark would be grateful if the party could ensure the refinery is restored and put back to work — the machine spirits should not be left to degrade in such a way. If the characters agree to help, Vark mentions that the ventilation shafts might provide a good vantage to survey the refinery itself, should they need to.

Interviewing Brandt Kesker

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Brandt Kesker} is the last thread they can chase before heading to the Refinery. Travelling to the Lower Hive from the Hive Spires takes the characters the better part of a day, so they may wish to prepare or rest before taking on the next part of the adventure. 

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} can be found in the crumbling habsprawls surrounding the Refinery, but it takes the characters some effort to locate him directly. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} has some idea of where he is — remember that she is accompanying the party or following them from the shadows. Otherwise, they’ll need to interview other citizens to find their way. They can make Challenging (+0) Logic (Investigation), Navigation (Surface), or Rapport (Inquiry) Tests to gather information. Failure means lost time, adding several hours to their search and may cause them to become Fatigued.

They should notice that many of the local citizens here are suffering from a disease, revealed to be known as Bloodlung. These inhabitants can be represented by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourers}, but they have an ongoing Poisoned (Minor) Condition. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} is in the final stages of the disease, lying on a bed of rags in the corner of a crowded hab. The other residents keep their distance, fearful of sharing his fate.

If asked about his supposed rebellion, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} says he got in trouble for daring to complain about the refinery conditions. He then escaped through one of the run-off pipes. His whole shift was dismissed as punishment. He doesn’t know who worked there afterwards, but is afraid they may have all perished there as the refinery is dangerously toxic. If the party can persuade him to speculate, he’ll tell them about the rumours that the whole place is staffed by mutants, but he finds this ridiculous, since surely even mutants can die.

Helping Kesker

If the characters can restore or shore up @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker}’s health, he is willing to accompany them to the manufactorum, usher them to the run-off pipe entrance and lead the characters around. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} is opposed to this, saying he’s in such bad shape he’ll die before even getting there. In truth, she wishes to stay in better control of the situation and views Kesker as a wild card. If the characters do accept Kesker’s help, he’ll die soon after the adventure concludes, but may sacrifice himself using his I’ll Die Trying Trait.

Rumours that players might hear from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker} or other locals are as follows:

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-tables.RollTable.No9sZ8JS0BvcygHQ noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Bloodlung

The lowliest inhabitants of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}are plagued with various conditions, infections, and diseases. Not all are named, but Bloodlung is well-known as a common affliction among refinery workers, likely as a result of their daily inhalation of poisonous vapours. The symptoms begin with a scratchy throat and dry cough, progress to painful, rattling lungs, and finally develop into a hacking, retching cough that brings up first blood, then partially dissolved lung tissue. Few live long after reaching this stage, and the Officio Medicae has no officially sanctioned cure.

If the characters spend too long in the refinery, they may begin to experience early symptoms themselves. If unprotected, after each encounter, characters should make a Difficult (−10) Fortitude (Endurance) Test. Any who fail become inflicted with the Poisoned (Minor) Condition for the remainder of the adventure, or until they receive treatment. Several quack cures are sold in the black markets of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}— some of these are useless but harmless, while others might make a character’s situation worse. It is at your discretion whether a character who tries one is cured or gains Corruption as a result.

Onto the Refinery

Maltus Refinery VI is within an hour’s walking distance of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Brandt Kesker}’s hab unit. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} can lead them there, or they can gain directions from local citizens. When they reach the refinery, read the following:

‘After pushing your way through the unwashed crowds of the Lower Hive, the sudden emptiness of the habways in front of Lord Felputh’s refinery is an ominous relief. Despite the distant rumble of the hive’s Generatorium, the manufactorum is unsettlingly quiet, embodied by a grave-like hush. Even with the refinery dormant, the heat remains intense, and the thick brownish air stings exposed skin. The ground is water-logged, and when flashes of the flickering lumens cast enough light, they reveal an oily scum floating on the surface. The towering iron gates rise before you, the welding that sealed them shut obvious from the lumpy scar of molten metal oozing and hardened through the gate’s central seal.’

The liquid at the characters’ feet is a corrosive but diluted acid. It’s essentially harmless, but it means there’s little evidence to find, other than some organic matter slowly melting that might once have been part of a limb. Examining the gates, they can make a Challenging (+0) Lore (Forbidden) Test to identify what has been scrawled upon them. What initially looks like rusted patches are in fact symbols painted in blood, in effigy of the eight-pointed mark of Chaos.

The gates are a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#barrier]{Barrier} that can be surmounted by a Hard (−20) Athletics (Climbing) Test or by dealing 20 Damage targeted at the welded area in the middle. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} discourages using this entry, as making any noise or climbing over might alert whatever is inside. This method causes a party of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} to attack soon after they enter the refinery.

If the characters heard about the ventilation shafts from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Vark} or the run-off pipes from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.npwGHKbHhFlY0A8u]{Kesker}, they can locate these entrances without the need for a Test. Otherwise, searching for one of these entrances requires making a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) or Navigation (Surface) Test. Failure means the party could take some Damage from traversing the area or alert the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} within if they make too much noise. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} is reluctant to help here, wary of dredging through the runoff, but follows the players if they find a way to enter.

pages.name: Part 2: The Refinery
pages.text:
Maltus Refinery VI is an enormous, ancient refinery in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} Lower Hive. The sprawling mass of furnaces, storage tanks, refining mechanisms and pumping stations is fully enclosed within its walls. There was no relief from the blistering heat, poisonous smoke, and thunderous noise while the manufactorum was in operation. Pipes and funnels carried away waste products, and the mysterious produce of its workings rolled out in barrels stamped with the Cog Mechanicum. The refinery operated monotonously for generations, regardless of the labourers who were mangled in its workings or died slowly of Bloodlung as they worked.

Though the refinery now lies quiet, the evidence of its centuries of industry shows everywhere. Every surface is thick with toxic filth, every pipe drips noxious fluids, or bears the strange whorls left by swirling gases. Some parts of the refinery are multi-levelled, standing on unsteady metal mesh floors, while other sections are more open, dominated by towering storage tanks or processing units. In some areas, lights are dim due to staining and corrosion, creating only a sickly orange glow. In others, there’s no light at all. Energy still being drawn from the Generatorum fizzes and pops among the refinery’s oily cogs and blood-stained wheels, vainly waiting for the machinery to move again.

If the party forced or surmounted the front gate to enter, they are immediately attacked by a horde of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} double the number of characters in the party. If broken open, a pair of Beastmen work to hastily re-seal or barricade the gates behind them.

If the characters entered via the , read the following:

‘After climbing up through the shafts, you reach an opening in the ceiling of the refinery and find yourself looking down at a gargantuan drum of black liquid. There appears to be no other way down other than by the rungs of a rusted ladder. Your hands have become coated in oily residue from the shaft, making it hard to grip; slipping here could be fatal.’

The characters must lower themselves 100 feet to land on a gangway; the ladder down is usable but slippery, requiring a Challenging (+0) Athletics (Climbing) Test. Any character who fails falls into one of the vats below, each full of an unpleasantly slimy, foul-smelling but harmless liquid. This fall shouldn’t inflict any Damage or Conditions, but feel free to improvise a drawback for failure. From there, climbing down to the refinery floor puts the players at the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1a.-wrecked-machinery-floor]{Wrecked Machinery Floor (1A)}.

If the players entered via the Run-off Pipes, read the following:

‘After trudging through the pipes, small enough that the tallest among you were forced to walk bent forward, you find yourselves in a large square container with a thick layer of neon purple sludge coating the metallic walls, and pooling at your feet.’

This container is 7 feet high, and the metallic walls have been reinforced with iron strips and thick bolts that make exiting an Easy (+40) Athletics (Climbing) Test. However, the purple slime is a poisonous residue. Unless the characters protect their flesh, each must make a Difficult (−10) Fortitude Test or receive the Poisoned (Minor) Condition for the next two hours. Exiting the container brings the characters next to the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1d.-desecrated-shrine]{Desecrated Shrine (1D)}.

Once in the refinery, distant explosions echo through the cavernous space. These are the result of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s agents cutting off their exits. The characters won’t discover this unless @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} becomes an ally and warns them, or they try to leave the refinery via the ventilation shafts or run-off pipes. They then find these destroyed, their exits irrevocably blocked.

Use the diagram to inform the characters of the nearest structures to their location so they can choose which areas to explore. Each labelled location is described in the following section. In addition, random encounter tables are also provided to increase the difficulty or extend the length of this part of the adventure. You may include as many or as few of these as necessary. The only information the players need to gain here is that the refinery is full of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} who worship Chaos, which should quickly become apparent.

If the players need reminding of their objective, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} can prompt them that they are there to establish what has taken over the refinery and halted its operation, so they can aid @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} in fixing the problem. Once they’ve seen @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}, however, Sandik’s objective is to trap or eliminate the characters and prevent them from exposing Lord Felputh’s shame. To conclude this part of the adventure, the characters must leave via the tunnel entrance at the north end of the refinery and enter the tunnels.

Sandik’s Mission

Once it’s clear that the characters are aware of the Chaos-worshipping Beastmen, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik} is on the lookout for a way to sabotage the party’s efforts in order to cover @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s tracks. She may alert a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} patrol to their presence and flee herself, activate some machinery while they’re inside, or attempt to meet with a character alone and attack them. How dangerous and effective her efforts are is up to you.

However, once the party knows of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Sandik}’s betrayal, she tries to save herself. In a pinch, she proposes a deal: If the party or their Patron can protect her from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh}, she’ll work with them, for at least as long as it takes to get out of the refinery.

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-tables.RollTable.10m912eLDoBpYITR noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Refinery Locations

During their traversal of the Maltus Refinery VI, be sure to convey to the party the sense of enormity within the facility and how multifaceted and confusing the surrounding machinery appears. The whole facility is littered with vats and broken machinery, and an eerie disquiet hangs in the air throughout, felt especially by any members of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus }present.

The party doesn’t need to visit all locations presented; be sure to lead them towards the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1e.-northern-tunnel-entrance]{Northern Tunnels Entrance (1E)} to enter the next section of the manufactorum. Use the encounters in the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-tables.RollTable.10m912eLDoBpYITR]{Maltus Refinery VI Encounters} Table to add complications to their travel between locations or punish them for failed Tests.

1A. Wrecked Machinery Floor

In this section of the manufactorum, most of the machinery has been damaged or destroyed. Investigating, it looks to have been battered and torn apart, and many pieces are missing. Characters can make a Hard (−20) Logic (Investigation) Test, depending on their successes, reveal to them the following clues:

  • 1–3 SL: A trail of wreckage leads north towards the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1e.-northern-tunnel-entrance]{Northern Tunnel Entrance (1E)}, via the @UUID[.vvoa9Cf947QMkVH8#1d.-desecrated-shrine]{Descecrated Shrine (1D)}. Whatever was taken from here was dragged there (material the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have used to create their cages and effigies in the tunnels).

    4–5 SL: Despite the wreckage, some tools and workbenches have been used recently. In particular, they find some long lengths of discarded metal that have been sharpened along one edge (some @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have been constructing their @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-items.Item.tqGb4ULjvQP5x7AK]{Herdcrafted Cleavers} in this area).

    6+ SL: If the characters are yet to discover the Beastmen, they find a chunk of organic material stuck between an array of wrecked cogs. Inspected further, this is revealed to be a tip of some animal’s horn, a strange thing to find on Voll altogether (part of a Beastman’s horn that broke off in the assault on the machinery).

1B. The Pens

A large cage made of bent girders and lengths of sharp wire has been built against the wall of an enormous vertical drainage pipe. Several figures are visible through the twisted metal, but only one is upright. This is Bek, who has only recently been captured (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourer} stat-block to represent him). He begs the party to save him, and if they refuse to help, he intentionally screams to alert a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} patrol. The other four Human captives are either close to death or mortally wounded.

If the characters have decided to look for missing citizens from the surrounding area (mentioned in a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-tables.RollTable.No9sZ8JS0BvcygHQ]{rumour}), they’ve been stored here. Bek has no idea what the Beastmen need them for; only that a captive is retrieved from the pen every day or so and taken further into the facility.

1C. The Furnaces

Three starved-looking @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} huddle by a small fire they’ve started, surrounded by the cavernous furnaces. If the characters watch and listen, these Beastmen bemoan that their brethren have turned to Chaos, and consider their options now. If a character succeeds on a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Charm) Test, these Beastmen can be talked to and give information to the players, but they are too afraid to enter the tunnels. Otherwise, these Beastmen flee rather than put up a fight and disappear into the manufactorum’s maze of machinery. 

Critical Information

Talking to any of the Beastmen at The Furnaces, or any the party encounters in the Tunnels (such as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.J8fomG1IJs18g3F5]{Gelka}, or even some exposition from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore}) reveals to the party pieces of how the Beastmen got to the refinery — their capture from a Feral World, their travel across the Void in a Rogue Trader’s voidship, and their subsequent arrival at Maltus Refinery VI. This is vital information to pass on to the characters, as it implicates @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}’s complicity. If they fail to retrieve this information from the NPCs, the characters should be able to recover shipping logs from cogitators and paper records kept in the refinery that line up with rumours and speculation they might have acquired earlier. Hard evidence may be required or at least reinforce how they wish to deal with Lord Felputh at the end of the adventure.

1D. Desecrated Shrine

At the centre of the refinery, a labourer’s shrine to the Glorious God-Emperor has been reduced to rubble. The party can spend an hour to restore the shrine, and all involved recover one spent Fate (or gain one temporary Fate they can spend but not burn, which they can use until the end of the adventure). They can also automatically pass the next Test they make to resist Corruption. 

They also notice hoofed footprints in the dust and rubble that seem to be heading north towards the tunnel entrance.

1E. Northern Tunnel Entrance

A tunnel entrance at the northern end of the refinery is guarded by a pair of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen}, ones loyal to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore}. A smeared trail of blood, left by bodies being dragged below, mars the entrance. Skulls, spikes and chaotic effigies surround the entrance, marking the tunnel entrance as the entrance to their territory.

Once the characters find a way past the Beastmen guards here, whether by defeating or distracting them and sneaking past, they enter the tunnels and the next part of the adventure.

pages.name: Part 3: The Tunnels
pages.text:
This part of the adventure is intended to be eerie and occasionally horrifying. Most of the tunnel areas are unlit, and the characters must find their own source of light or navigate in darkness. The tunnels should feel maze-like and unfathomable.

Characters would be advised to hide from or flee some of the encounters here. There are many hiding places in the tunnels, crevices to squeeze into, debris to hide under or behind. In some places, pipelines or wires run across the ceilings as a reminder of the refinery above, and offer a handhold if characters need to hide in a hurry.

Various threats roam freely, you can introduce locations and random encounters as required (see the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-tables.RollTable.jBVqRmfuErptNaGv]{Maltus Refinery VI Tunnel Encounter}s Table). The characters should be able to avoid some of these encounters if they’re careful; the only encounter they cannot avoid is with the Beastmen Shaman @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} in The Shaman’s Lair (2E), lying between them and the last remaining exit.

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-tables.RollTable.jBVqRmfuErptNaGv noCenter=true description=bottom]{Rumour}

Tunnel Locations

The tunnels under Maltus Refinery VI are many and winding, a criss-crossing tangle of metallic walkways, rocky burrows and crumbling foundations, often interspersed with reaches of acidic runoff from the manufactorum above. It’s a maddening warren, home to the Chaos-worshipping Beastmen, and perhaps older, stranger foes.

2A. Northern Tunnel Exit

As the party enters the tunnels, read the following:

‘The tunnels slope down, far below the refinery. It’s dark and humid, the rough walls dripping moisture. Every sound echoes, so each single drip or footstep sounds like many. It would be easy to lose your way in these tunnels, and wander forever through the blackness.’

Each character can make a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) or (Hearing) or Intuition (Surroundings) Test to detect two potential ways forward. A blood trail leads to @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2b.-mesks-cage]{Mesk’s Cage (2B)}, and the sound of far-off chanting and flickers of light point towards the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2c.-beastmens-ritual]{Beastemen’s Ritual (2C)}. If everyone fails their Test, the party might stumble into either encounter, and any enemies could gain the drop on them. 

2B. Mesk’s Cage

The former leader of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} is trapped in a cage, suspended from the ceiling of an unlit cavern. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} lies weakly at the bottom of the cage, clothed in thin rags, his limbs dangling in the air. He’s battered and starving, and he’s given up any hope of rescue. He believes all the Beastmen have embraced Chaos, and he’s just waiting to die.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} willingly answers any questions he can, but doesn’t plead for help. He has given up, and unless a loyal member of the herd is with the characters, the only way to help him is to appeal towards his deeper desire for revenge. The thought of sticking a knife into @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgor}e’s back would be a moment worth living for. If the characters rescue @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} and outfit him with a weapon, they gain +1 Superiority for the upcoming encounter in the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2e.-the-shamans-lair]{Shaman’s Lair (2E)}. 

The cage is made from old pipes and strips of metal scavenged from the refinery and is suspended via a heavy chain passed over a rusty girder. Lowering the cage safely requires making a Hard (−20) Athletics (Might) Test, wherein each character involved lowers the Difficulty of the Test by 1 step. If the chain is broken or the cage dropped, it splits open when it hits the ground, dealing 5 Damage to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk}.

Herdcrafted Cleaver

Many of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} carry weapons they’ve made themselves in the refinery, using shards of metal broken from the dormant machinery and whatever other materials they can find. With fires and forges at their disposal, these cleavers are well-made in a style familiar to the Beastmen. They function as large knives and are used to fight, butcher meat, or make sacrifices to Chaos.

These cleavers would be considered an unusual item in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} black markets, so they are Scarce. Arming @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} with a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-items.Item.tqGb4ULjvQP5x7AK]{Herdcrafted Cleaver}, if the characters have recovered one, would remind him of his former pride in his Herd and make him a willing ally when fighting @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Talgore}.

2C. Beastmen’s Ritual

Strange guttural chanting echoes from the tunnel’s walls, and a flickering red glow casts deep, squirming shadows up ahead. If the players continue, they find a chamber ablaze with thick brown candles that fill the air with a meaty stench. A pair of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.TRcwwntLPqt7KaJy]{Mutated Beastmen} wearing hoods over their horned heads are circling a similarly hooded figure on its knees in the centre of the chamber. Its hands, bound behind it, look distinctly Human, as do its bare and bloodied feet. The chanting Mutated Beastmen are preparing their blades, whetting them and wiping them down as best they can. This unfortunate victim is an unwilling part of some tainted ritual, awaiting the attention of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Shaman}.

If the players rescue the victim, the hood comes off, and the figure is revealed to have the horns and bovine features of the Beastmen, although there’s still something Human about them. They can’t speak but only bray mournfully, and if left alive, run off into the tunnels (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZUWBWGM4eH7xFZ8P]{Dreg} stat-block to represent this pitiful creature).

2D. Acynadi Den

The tunnels open up into a shallow cavern waterlogged by acidic runoff. Strangely, signs of life among the pools — clusters of sizable dormant @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{acynadi }— are visible. Rusted pipes run through the cavern, boiling the runoff into steam that fills the chamber. The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} have been harvesting them as an additional source of meat.

If the characters succeed at a Difficult (−10) Stealth (Move Silently) Test, they pass unharmed through the chamber. For each character who fails, the party is attacked by one @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ZIxRrvXoXCRKAYyI]{Acynadi Delta-5}. If all characters fail, they are attacked by an @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.8dS1s1UvVXyt6dyv]{Acynadi Gamma-7} instead.

The entire chamber is Difficult Terrain. If any of the pipes is damaged, the related Zone becomes a Minor Hazard. Passing through the acynadi den allows the characters to enter the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2e.-the-shamans-lair]{Shaman’s Lair (2E)} from a point of vantage, also granting them +1 Superiority in the upcoming encounter. However, they do not gain this Superiority if they use any Loud weaponry or equipment in the chamber.

2E. The Shaman’s Lair

The Beastmen Shaman @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} conducts unholy rites in his gruesome lair. Here, the air smells of sulphur and blood, and any Psykers in the party can feel the painful, maddening presence of Chaos nipping at them from the Warp. The lair is cluttered with empty crates that serve as furniture, barrels with dismembered limbs protruding from the top, and odd items taken from the refinery or stolen from the nearest habsprawls: bits of old machinery, a broken cart, piles of rags, all items the party might use as cover if they seek to enter the lair unseen. These are scattered all over the Lair, with four surrounding Zones and a central Zone as follows.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Talgore} has also had his followers erect a false herdstone in the centre of the cavern, a great lump of rock into which they’ve carved Chaos symbols, before pouring the blood of sacrifices into the grooves. A Human corpse lies drained and dead at its base. This stone is a source of Corruption — characters who end their turn within this central Zone make a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Psychic) Test to resist 1 Corruption Point. Making physical contact with the stone is Moderate Exposure, requiring a Challenging (+0) Fortitude Test to resist 2 Corruption Points. Every SL reduces the number of Corruption Points gained by 1. Damaging the false herdstone at the beginning of the encounter, or during, grants the party +1 Superiority.

If the party enters without @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Talgore}’s knowledge, they see him sprinkling clouds of corrosive chemical dust, taken from the refinery, over herdstone and followers alike. This hisses on contact, singeing the fur and skin of those it lands on, but they don’t react. Talgore mutters as he works, invoking the gods of Chaos, and preaching to his followers. Some of what he says sound like grunts or wordless bellows to the characters, but some they can understand:

‘Rise up! Show them your strength! Death to humans and glory for the Herd!’

There is a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastman} here for every character (including allied NPCs), plus the Shaman @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} himself. While the party may enter unseen, passing to the exit at the far end of the chamber, beyond the Shaman’s makeshift throne, is difficult. It is possible to escape without fighting the Shaman, and there are a number of Hazards that might be used to the character’s advantage:

  • The barrel of chemical dust near the Shaman could be upturned over a character to cause 10 Damage, or knocked over to cause 5 Damage to all opposing characters within Close Range.

  • Any @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} allies are sickened by the perversion they see here and cannot resist attacking the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Shaman} outright. This should keep him occupied for a few turns.

  •  A crazed @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultist} has been chained, unarmed, to one of the walls. It strains at its bonds, reaching its grasping tentacles towards whoever comes nearest, herd or Human doesn’t matter to this maddened creature. If released, it attacks indiscriminately, and may seek to escape backwards in the tunnels.

If the characters left the two @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.TRcwwntLPqt7KaJy]{Mutated Beastmen} undisturbed at the @UUID[.zxtdKCbEeChB51rY#2c.-beastmens-ritual]{Beastmen’s Ritual (2C)}, they’ll join the fight four rounds in, after hearing any commotion.

After the encounter, a tunnel at the back of the Shaman’s Lair can take them back to the Lower Hive, a hidden exit just outside the area surrounding the manufactorum, bypassing the closed-off entrances behind them in the upper floors. If they go back and aim to exit from the refinery’s gates, they’re still sealed, and a band of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.bB0rMr6Gez3M9bME]{Gangers} wait to ambush them — paid off by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} to ensure no one escapes.

Dealing with Lord Felputh

The adventure’s conclusion lies with how the party seeks to deal with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}. If @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} becomes an ally, she offers to arrange a meeting with Lord Felputh, or they may seek to return to the Hive Spires of their own accord. The party has some time to prepare, since everyone has been convinced they’ve become blockaded within the manufactorum.

Exposing Felputh: If the characters reveal that not only did @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} bring @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} into work in his factory, but that those Beastmen corrupted Human labourers and spread Chaos, then he’s likely to lose everything, including his life.

If he can convince the party to lie about what they’ve seen, and let him spread the word that his problems are caused by rampant mutancy in the surrounding habsprawls, nothing to do with him at all, he can call for the whole area to be purged and no one would ever know he was to blame.

The characters may accept a bribe of 1000 solars each to keep @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh}’s secret. Whether the party’s Patron would approve of their choice depends on their faction and motivations, so the players may have to consider keeping this secret from their Patron. 

Punishing Felputh: Alternatively, the party may be determined to bring @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} to justice, either of their own making or by informing the Macharian Vigilites or an agent of the Inquisition of the Chaos worship going on under his watch. In this case, the refinery is purged, the tunnels sealed off, and a new noble takes over his holdings, taking on the burden of repairs so the refinery is soon operational again.

pages.name: Aftermath
pages.text:
After dealing with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, there are a few more points worth wrapping up with the party.

Releasing any captured locals from the refinery causes the remaining manufactorum labourers to thank the characters in the streets of the Lower Hive for this miracle, offering them scraps of food and shelter if needed. The characters have given the citizens hope, and are local heroes for a while. 

If the characters decide to free the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} (led by @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.YWOtDHG1vScQKCB4]{Mesk} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.J8fomG1IJs18g3F5]{Gelka} if they survive the final encounter), they take the chance to disappear from the refinery and seek a better life elsewhere.
