They might scrape a living in the Bowels of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, competing with gangers who see them only as monsters, or perhaps they take to the acidic wilds beyond, their hardier stature proving more adaptable to the world’s hostile environments.

Some NPCs the characters encountered could become valuable Contacts or Hirelings in their future adventures, such as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.fdJv9lqD4Nr2SAQz]{Magos Elipses Vark} (if they managed to liberate the manufactorum), @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.0zWbIXfmA6absQL7]{Kant Sandik} (who would make an excellent guide to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}), and even @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} may become a Contact if the characters dealt with him favourably at the end, or hold significant blackmail over his head.

Experience Points

All characters should earn @Reward[xp=30 reason=Paradigm Shift]{30 XP} for participating in the adventure, but if any characters achieved personal goals or fulfilled a goal for a Patron their reward should be increased accordingly. In addition, the following experience can be awarded:

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Deduced the presence of Beastmen]{10 XP} for deducing the presence of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} before encountering them. 

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Gained ally]{10 XP} for each ally gained during the mission, whether the ally survived or not.

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Navigated the refinery using stealth]{10 XP} for navigating the refinery using stealth,

  • @Reward[xp=30 reason=Defeated Arkt Talgore]{30 XP} for defeating @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore}, the Beastmen Shaman.

Influence

Award or reduce the character's Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} if they successfully liberated the Refinery from the Beastmen, or negatively if they sided with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} in the end and the manufactorum is purged. Consider Influence gains with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}, Macharian Vigilites (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}), or nobility of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, depending on how they dealt with Felputh in the end; rumours travel fast in Rokarth, so any public resolution is bound to garner attention from the related factions.

These increases can bleed over to their Patron’s Influences if they represented their Patron honourably or made such a gross error in judgment as to affect their Patron’s standings. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

If the characters fail to complete the main objectives of the adventure, the powers at play escalate their operations.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} gets away with using the characters as pawns. After some time, he attempts to pin the blame on the party and their Patron. He claims their interference led to the Beastmen infestation and has doctored communiques linking them to the Klaskoloff Dynasty’s contact.

But in that time, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.FS6l4jv4KbzBf89s]{Arkt Talgore} is left to continue his experiments. He creates more mutants that spread into the surrounding hab blocks, rampantly killing citizens and spreading Warp phenomena. He turns Maltus Refinery VI into a massive source of corruption, eventually gaining the attention of a daemon of Tzeentch, creating a foothold for daemonic influence in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}.

Eventually, Maltus Refinery VI and the surrounding hab blocks are marked as condemned, and operations to purge the area begin, resulting in a long and costly battle between the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.actors.Actor.O49jTi2TzoFQH5GT]{Macharian Vigilites}. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh} is relieved of his duty to oversee the manufactorum, but manages to save face in the courts of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}and the last dregs of his fortune. The former workers are reassigned to new duties across Voll, and many families are broken up as a result. 

If the characters are still alive and somehow escape Maltus Refinery VI, Felputh eventually learns they survived and seeks to kill them. He’ll send gangers and assassins, though his reach cannot extend beyond Voll’s system.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • After some time, any survivors from the refinery may begin to manifest Chaos mutations and attack their kin. The locals around the refinery beg the characters to hunt the mutant down. They could be hiding anywhere in the Lower Hive of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, or have retreated into the Bowels; regardless, they leave a trail of destruction and phenomena that makes them easy to follow. Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultist} stat-block to represent these mutants. The locals can’t offer material rewards for this task, but they could gain Influence and Contacts with the Inquisition by showing their effectiveness.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.J8fomG1IJs18g3F5]{Gelka} and the Beastmen could ask the characters to help her and her herd find a way off Voll, or at least out of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. If the characters successfully aid Gelka, she becomes a Contact. Alternatively, the party could alert the local Vigilites, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}, or even @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} to the Beastmen’s attempt to flee, and gain an additional +1 Influence with one of those factions.

  • Whether the party accepts or denies @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Felputh}’s bribe, if left alive, he becomes increasingly paranoid that they’ll reveal his secret anyway. He squanders the remains of his wealth to send a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5a6Q3NRdPonZjiGr]{Death Cult Assassin} after the characters.

pages.name: Getting Started
pages.text:
The adventure begins with the characters receiving a message and accompanying papers from their Patron. The characters are assumed to already be in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, but their Patron’s message could reach them elsewhere if necessary and direct them to Voll’s capital. Depending on the Patron, this might come via a written message slipped under a door, delivered by a Servo-Skull, or some other means.

Considering the Patron’s origins and motivations, you may wish to adapt the following text before reading aloud:

‘I have arranged for you to meet Lord Felputh and provided you with the necessary papers. This minor noble has had trouble overseeing his manufactorum. It has ceased operations, risking Rokarth’s fulfilment of the tithe. Your task is to establish the nature of the problem for Lord Felputh and offer him guidance so that he can rectify the situation. Additionally, you should determine the extent of the noble’s failings and report back to me. The affairs of Rokarth’s elite are rarely simple, and knowledge of his affairs might prove valuable.’

Patrons

There might be many reasons why the characters’ Patron sends them to meet @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}. The noble may have contacted the Patron for aid, or the Patron has their own motivation for interfering, and the noble remains ignorant of their interest until the players arrive. The following are suggestions for each Patron Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: If the Patron is Tithe Prefectus, then @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} likely begged them for mercy, afraid he would be unable to meet his quota. In this case, he had no choice but to agree to the players’ visit, but received them reluctantly.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: Aware of the true purpose of Maltus Refinery VI and its mysterious product, the Patron knows it’s paramount that the refinery resumes production. This information is highly classified, something the party will never know.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: Magos Vark alerted the Patron to the situation, and no member of the Adeptus Mechanicus is comfortable with the thought that Maltus Refinery VI remain unused. Imperial machinery must be maintained to serve its purpose, and this manufactorum is in dire need of attention.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} was once known for his generosity to the Ministorum, but as his fortunes have fallen, his faith too seems to have waned. Recognising his ancestral house, the Patron intends to give the lord a chance to redeem himself and set the situation right.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: What seems a minor inconvenience today, a few snatched citizens or a minor rebellion among manufactorum workers, might become a significant threat to the Imperium tomorrow.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: Any situation that affects the regular flow of goods to and from @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}is likely to catch the attention of the party’s Patron. Significant disruption along the supply chain could eventually impact the imperial fleet’s departure schedules.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: The Patron has identified @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} as a potential ally, customer, or target of extortion. Even a minor noble has wealth and connections that could prove useful, and this one is clearly desperate.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: No one is above the Inquisition, and whatever the Patron’s Ordo they’ve been watching @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} from afar for some time. When a noble becomes desperate they’re most likely to succumb to the many vices and temptations of the Imperium’s enemies. If there is evidence of corruption in the refinery, its owner must be held responsible.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasty:} While it’s not for the players to know, their Patron’s Dynasty or connections played a part in arranging the mysterious shipment that brought @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} his new workforce. By sending the players to investigate, their Patron hopes to demonstrate their own innocence.

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: If @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} cannot keep the refinery operational, then he has already failed in his duty to the God-Emperor. The situation should be swiftly rectified, the noble’s infirmities exposed, and normal operations restored.

  • Information: Knowledge is power, and power over a noble, even one as minor as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh}, is desirable. This Patron may rather prevent the lord’s fall for the moment. He may have assets, contacts, and inside knowledge of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} noble houses worth extracting first.

  • Materiel: The Patron may take a personal interest in the produce of the refinery, and the wealth it brings its owner. Holding leverage over @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BMt1lzDVRMWAsuQk]{Lord Felputh} is appealing, or — if the Patron has the power to do so — confiscating the refinery might be preferable.

  • Reputation: The greater the degradation of the refinery, the more appealing its restoration to Imperial greatness. If Chaos, xenos, or some other foul enemy of the Imperium has taken root, purging that enemy should bolster the Patron’s reputation, especially if the situation is dire.

  • Unity: Everything about this case makes the Patron uncomfortable. Tithes should not go unfulfilled, refineries should not lie unused, and nobles of any sort should not sink below their station. The Patron won’t be satisfied until the status quo is restored.

pages.name: Implacable
pages.text: Implacable takes place throughout the Lower Hive sectors of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, drawing characters into a plot of widespread murder and heretical cult activity, masterminded by an unlikely and deadly foe. Implacable can serve as a stand-alone experience played over 2–3 sessions or, should they survive, as part of a extensive campaign.

pages.name: Adventure Overview
pages.text:
In Implacable, the characters must end a series of bloody massacres that have disrupted a large swath of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, endangering the Tithe and imperilling a significant local festival celebrating the founding of Voll. The party’s Patron has been asked to assist in the situation, partly because the perpetrator is seemingly far more deadly than even the already fearful populace of the hive knows.

@UUID[.PsmOAhxxerPsny8D]{Part 1: Faltering Tithe} — The adventure opens with the characters receiving their assignment from their Patron, with orders to find and stop the culprit behind the massacres that have disrupted production in the eastern Lower-Hive quarters of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. They are introduced to their Macharian Vigilite liaison, Captain Vern. They are given the few clues that have been gathered so far and given the choice to either meet or ignore Master Nixious Morlay, who is eager to assist in their efforts. 

@UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV]{Part 2: Strange Patterns} — The characters have the opportunity to follow up on promising leads, including potentially studying the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}’s records, questioning the survivor of a Harbinger attack, and inspecting the gruesome recent aftermath of a Harbinger-style massacre.

@UUID[.d03FcrEvHxHGZlE9]{Part 3: Ragged Faith }— The characters are ambushed by the ‘Harbinger’ and some of his faithful acolytes, the Vertexis cult, testing their might and cunning head-on against this strange new foe. It may appear as if their job is now complete.

@UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records }— Yet certain facts suggest the characters’ task is incomplete, though they’ve been congratulated and encouraged to move on. It falls to Loga Binary-46 to convince them, if needed, that all is not well. They journey to @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Crystalline Reflectory, bastion of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica, to follow their new lead.

@UUID[.UHtSqeiaUMvo4YMP]{Part 5: The Apocalypse Nears} — The characters face a phenomenally deadly foe in a desperate bid to stop their ploy to kill tens of millions of citizens. Their options have narrowed to a handful of decisive outcomes.

@UUID[.KqNEqbvK8OPcKBwf]{Aftermath} — The characters may have saved the day, rescuing millions of lives who will never know their names, and@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} along with it. The status quo is maintained, and Voll’s tithe contributions get back on track. Otherwise, backlash from their failures could plunge Rokarth into darkness and dethrone it as Voll’s capital hive.

Caelius's Legacy

The High Lords of Terra are not known for their mercy. In the wake of the Macharian Heresy to demonstrate the price of turning against the Imperium, they took particular note of Marshal Surlan Caelius. A charismatic and rebellious figure, Caelius had fought on against the Imperium even after the death of his commander, General Lysander. It was not Marshal Caelius’ military skills that truly condemned him, though — it was the soaring rhetoric with which he made a continual and articulate case for rebellion against an Imperium he declared unjust.

Even though his insurgency had been crushed, and the Marshal reportedly wounded, the High Lords turned to one of their most reliable tools and dispatched an Imperial Assassin to eliminate not only Caelius but his entire household. The Marshal’s flight was traced to the then recently founded hive world of Voll, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} in particular, as he sought to hide amongst the teeming pilgrim masses. Considering what had been sent after him, Caelius’s cowardly ploy would have served the heretic poorly, but the Warp is fickle, and the assassin’s transport vessel was lost on its journey to Voll.

Marshal Caelius never faced the justice he deserved, and lived out the rest of his long life in unearned safety, amidst a large family that knew barely anything of his previous crimes against the Imperium.

Over five centuries later, in the wake of the opening of the Cicatrix Maledictum, a heavily damaged Imperial vessel with no discernible markings emerged from the Warp, bearing a lone surviving passenger in cryo-stasis, locked within a single-occupant drop pod. The ship arrived within the Voll System and initiated crash procedures even as it hurtled toward the planet. The small crew of servitors aboard the vessel launched the drop pod only moments before uncontrolled entry into Voll’s atmosphere tore the voidship to pieces.

It did not take long for the newly activated assassin to tap into @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} datacrypts in search of his assigned targets. Over half a millennium later, Marshal Caelius’ descendants numbered close to a million, giving or taking several thousand lost to the Adeptus Administratum’s arcane bureaucracy.

An Imperial Assassin now hunts the habways and spires of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, his Sentinel Array noting faint traces of Caelius’ genetic signature in endless crowds of people throughout the hive’s eastern quarter. If he had originated from a different Assassinorum Temple, perhaps he would’ve sought clarification on his mission, but he is an Eversor. Gene-altered to inhuman combat prowess and psycho-conditioned to be utterly without remorse or pity, Eversor Assassins do not exist merely to kill. Their purpose is to annihilate, to terrify, to show heretics that the Wrath of the God-Emperor is entirely without limits or mercy.  

The Eversor has never received counter-orders, so the mission stands: eradicate Caelius and his entire household… no matter how large it may be.

Hands of Death

Within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, buried beneath layers of bureaucratic meandering and deliberate obfuscation, there lies a body dedicated to swift, inevitable, and efficient disposal of any target. The Officio Assassinorum has a range of assets for whom the art of death is not merely a martial virtue, but an irresistible spiritual calling. Within the halls of its assorted temples are crafted killers beyond compare. They are masters of stealth, equipped with ruinous weaponry and hideous toxins, each capable of unparalleled bloodshed inflicted in countless ways. Each is pushed past the boundaries of average Human capability by augmetics, medicae drugs and combat stimms to hone their brutal efficiency. They are a horror most citizens of the Imperium have no idea exist, and would count themselves lucky never to share a planet with.

Nevertheless, countless billions owe their lives to the secret acts of these brutal assassins. Though few official records exist, these unheralded agents of the God-Emperor’s will have slain corrupt planetary governors, executed xenos generals, and laid waste to nascent cults that would have offered up whole worlds to their dark gods. 

Of all the tools crafted by the Officio Assassinorum, the Eversor is perhaps the least subtle. The Eversor Temple believes that the best way to eliminate a target is in a blaze of psychotic fury, disregarding factors such as collateral damage, practicality or the potential innocence of bystanders. Eversor Assassins are locked in cryo-stasis and, when active, only kept in check by mission parameters delivered via cranial augmetics. Once roused, potent combat stimms drive them to superhuman levels of speed, strength and aggression. Chosen targets have little chance of survival against such a ruthless foe, and any who come between them will meet the same brutal end.

Failing Quotas

Murder is all too common in any hive city — a certain incidence count is expected and accounted for by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}. Indeed, a (rare) subsidence in the rate of homicide generally leads to a momentary increase in the number of soldiers tithed to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}, and a good deal of paperwork to accompany it. The majority of deaths within @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} are commonly attributed to gang violence, summary justice from various enforcers, industrial accidents, Infractionist activity, or a bored nobility in search of bloody diversion. Thus, a long series of grisly murders occurring throughout Rokarth’s eastern quarter went unremarked by the Macharian Vigilites, given the gargantuan population density and scale of the districts involved. All until the data points related to the murders began to match up. 

Over several months, the murders grew increasingly grisly and became increasingly associated with nearby industrial accidents, which further investigation showed were clearly sabotage. A newly reconsecrated cathedrum wall collapsed, killing hundreds. An entire manufactorum shift was slain by an explosively rerouted acid wash. Even the ordinary citizenry of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, rarely informed of goings-on far beyond their hab, began to take notice. They slowly discerned that they were being targeted and grew increasingly fearful. This has led to a notable decrease in productivity throughout the eastern hive, though some imaginative overseers fear it may lead to far worse than that. This, at last, drew the attention of both the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum }and @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{House Castyx} — for there is nothing of greater importance on Voll than the sanctity of the Tithe, especially after the dark and unproductive years of the Noctis Aeterna.

With increased scrutiny came a name for this supposed perpetrator.

The Harbinger 

Hivers throughout @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}claim to have caught glimpses of a dark, deathly figure flitting through the habs and manufactorums where sabotage occurred, as have the few rare survivors of its attacks. A small, but growing, cult — the Vertexis — claims that the figure is an angel of the God-Emperor, bringing His righteous judgement against the many sinners of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} (ironically, not an entirely incorrect sentiment). They refer to the dark angel as the Harbinger, and they have begun to graffiti murals depicting his pale face with various exhortations — the most common being simply ‘Judgment is Coming’. Many are unhinged fanatics and may potentially attack anyone they perceive as being out to stop the Harbinger from purging @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} sins. 

Witnesses’ descriptions of the Harbinger have a few consistencies — all note a sinister, swift-moving figure clad in black with a terrible, gaunt, pale face and burning eyes. Some claim the eyes glowed a deep crimson, others a pale blue. A few stated that the figure wielded a scythe that could shear through an armoured bulkhead like it was paper. A widely circulating rumour says a group of Macharian Vigilites nearly caught the Harbinger in a trap, and it killed most of them in return. The Harbinger is, in part, the Eversor Assassin codenamed Interitas. But very few witnesses remain of his true work. Most witnesses related to the investigation have observed a copycat killer instead, a death cultist masquerading as something far more, whom the characters will invariably meet during their investigation.

Interitas has experienced rare frustration in his present mission. Cracking into @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} datavaults, he recognised that the sheer volume of targets would take him a thousand years to eliminate by traditional linear means. He is frenzied by the fluctuating number of targets: knowing the longer he takes to complete his task, the more he has to eradicate, and so many have already lived full lives escaping the God-Emperor’s wrath. One detail of note is that most of his targets dwell in the eastern Lower Hive sectors of Rokarth, though scattered across its many levels. With a relatively compact zone for such a large number of targets, the necessary slaughter can be perpetrated with utmost efficiency.

Not long after the characters begin their investigation, news of an upcoming event in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} leads the assassin to modify his tactics once more, as he suspects a massive amount of his targets will assemble into a single hive buttress, affording him a unique opportunity to eliminate a considerable portion of them at once during the festival known as Halion’s Triumph. There is sure to be significant collateral damage.

Halion’s Triumph

One of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} most critical civic commemorations, Halion’s Triumph, celebrates the official founding of Voll and is marked by a vast series of feasts. Each decade, on the day of Halion’s Triumph, workers are rewarded with their share of a grand feast at the end of their shifts, provided they meet the day’s quota. @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.Kz0WP5E5hu0eHF4O#the-acynadi]{Acynadi} meat is served on behalf of the commemoration’s patrons, a joint venture between @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{House Castyx} and the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#carnem]{Mercator Carnem} — the Meat Guild of Voll. 

The Halion’s Triumph feasts are one of the few times many of Voll’s hivers will ever get to taste meat in their entire lives, and all inhabitants of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} highly anticipate the day. The population of Rokarth is such that many thousands of feasts of varying sizes occur across the hive over an entire day, with a few notable locations hosting feasts for many thousands of clamouring, hungry citizens.

The Frantic Official

Master Nixious Morlay is a high-level agent of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, though firmly allied with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#carnem]{Mercator Carnem}. Master Morlay’s entire existence revolves around Halion’s Triumph. It takes nearly ten whole years since the last festival to plan for the next, and this is the third Triumph that Morlay has been responsible for overseeing. The predations of the Harbinger have now caused what is all but unthinkable to Morlay: various Factions within @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} quietly suggest that the festival should be postponed, or even entirely cancelled, until the threat to production is dealt with. He is, however, determined that the massive festival goes forward as is tradition. The characters are tasked to stop the Harbinger's plans by Morlay and his hysterical requests for immediate support in handling the increasingly dire situation.

Should the characters choose to help him, they find Morlay an overanxious but ostensibly well-meaning ally, eager to assist their investigations in any way he can, while constantly requesting updates on their activities. The Master is assisted by a cadre of iridescently jacketed enforcers from the Mercator Carnem who do his bidding, assisting the characters as requested. Drawing on Morlay’s Influence can open certain doors, though not without a cost; however, at the midpoint of Implacable, once the characters have apparently dealt with the Harbinger — though in fact have merely stopped a copy-cat killer — and the brutal murders have suddenly stopped, Morlay is all-too-eager to profusely thank the characters for their efforts and send them away. He is stubbornly unwilling to look at evidence suggesting the Harbinger hasn’t truly been dealt with, and his enforcers turn their aggression onto the characters if they persist in their investigations against the Master’s orders, hampering their efforts.

Festivals in the Imperium

Repeated @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} analysis points to consistent productivity spikes surrounding extended periods of annual worship and observances. Therefore, worldwide and hive-wide commemorations are curated in each world’s calendar to give workers moments of collective pride and subservience — all practical efforts in raising @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} regiments to defend the Imperium and provide the populace a sense of purpose in their backbreaking toil. Even if such festivals are barely concealed propaganda, designed to stir religious zeal, martial pride or appeal to the legions of workers, acknowledging the contributions of their toil.

Masters of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} are assigned to work with Planetary Governors, or their representatives, to coordinate these massive festivals and occasional entertainments. These are often accompanied by processions, parades, and carefully negotiated breaks from labour, often followed by extraneous overtime to make up for and exceed the brief dip in production. Some feature occasional feasts, among the only times in their lives that most hive citizens get to taste anything other than remanufactured nutrient pastes that are a staple of hive life.

pages.name: Getting Started
pages.text:
The adventure begins with the characters already situated in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, perhaps wrapping up the loose ends of one of the other missions within Voll Adventures. When the party is gathered in a relatively secluded location, an ornate and heavily scrimshawed servo-skull approaches them and begins relaying an urgent message from their Patron. 

Read or paraphrase the following text:

‘A suddenly pressing matter needs your immediate attention. What were once thought to be random acts of murder and sabotage occurring throughout the eastern portion of Rokarth have been linked to a growing heretical cult known as the Vertexis. They supposedly worship a figure known as the Harbinger whom they dare claim is an angel of the Emperor and say is responsible for the violence. Many workers have apparently grown so fearful of this Harbinger that production has greatly slowed and the Tithe is endangered.

Find this Harbinger, discover its nature, and eliminate it. There is a contact who has earned my trust, Captain Matis Vern, a Vigilite who can give you more information to direct your efforts. Seek him in the East Wing, Block 3, of the Precinct Fortress Majoris. There are conduct passes within this servo-skull to grant you access to the fortress.

Blasphemy cannot be tolerated. Neither can failure. May His will light your way.’

The characters have some time to prepare, gather equipment, or anything else they think they might need for the mission ahead, before heading to Precinct Fortress Majoris.

Identity and Authorisations

The players may wish to work out what their character’s cover for this investigation will be, though this may well be influenced by whatever past relationship they’ve developed with @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Macharian Vigilites}. Worth noting is that the passes which their Patron has bequeathed to the characters bear the symbol of Voll’s Ruling House Castyx and give access to not only the fortress but authorization to ride a private Maglift within the hive’s central Maglev Nexus to it — consider how their Patron came upon these passes. An Inquisitor Patron could have simply demanded them, whereas an Infractionsit Patron may have spent a considerable sum of solars to create forgeries.

Patrons

This adventure has many hooks that can draw the attention of any type of Patron. The following are suggestions for each Patron Faction:

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}: Your Patron is concerned for the state of the Imperial Tithe, especially since the Macharian Sector is still in the midst of recovery from the dark years of the Noctis Aeterna. Anything that jeopardises @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} tithe must be eliminated as quickly as possible.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}: The disruption caused by the nightmares of the fearful populace of Rokarth resonates in the Warp and has dramatically affected its psykers. Your Patron believes that the sooner the mass murders stop, the quicker the immaterium calms and the psykers’ headaches will cease.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}: Your Patron suspects that the brutal and ruthless efficiency of the killings suggests work of an advanced combat servitor. It must be captured so its corrupted machine spirit can be purged and reconsecrated towards more righteous purposes.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}: Your Patron is deeply concerned by tales of citizens worshipping this Harbinger as an angel of the Emperor. This heretical cult, the Vertexis, must be crushed quickly, lest it grow further. Stopping the figure behind their idolatry is the best way to return everyone to the light of the Imperial Creed.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}: @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} is a large producer of medicae drugs for the entire sector, which Astra Militarum regiments greatly need and are already short on. Anything that hampers production is a concern worth dealing with from your Patron’s point of view, to say nothing of the fact that they suspect the killings and sabotage may be direct enemy activity, a possibility that must be investigated.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet}: The smooth flow of goods is essential to both mercantile and naval concerns throughout the Macharian Sector. Your Patron is greatly troubled that Voll’s supply chain can be disrupted by apparently a single individual and wants the matter resolved quickly.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}: Your Patron explains that the Harbinger is bad for business. A little fear can motivate, but terror keeps citizens indoors, preventing them from partaking in illicit goods and services. Worse, the Vigilites are cracking down even more brutally than normal and demanding even higher bribes due to the danger.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.41XgDdxnZ76elnvr]{Inquisition}: The brutal killings reported so far could draw the attention of Inquisitors from any Holy Order. It could be the work of daemons, a vile heretic cult, or proof that a xenos entity has infiltrated @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}.

  • @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.h6Z6Ia2q5RkRUlDG]{Rogue Trader Dynasties}: Your Patron is convinced that something escaped from the hold of a voidship that must be stopped, or seeks to gain a favour from House Castyx by taking care of their production problem.

Depending on a Patron’s Motivation, the following may also be suitable:

  • Conflict: Kill the Harbinger and hunt down any accomplices, including its burgeoning cult.

  • Information: Discover exactly who and what the Harbinger is, who sent it, and what their motivations were. 

  • Materiel: Seize any unusual equipment the Harbinger has access to and claim a portion of the goods, the flow of which is made possible by its elimination.

  • Reputation: Permanently stop the killings, and make it clear to all of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth} who eliminated what was hunting them.

  • Unity: Stop the Harbinger, making certain to involve agents of the Administratum and the Vigilites so all can claim they had a part in ending its brutal attacks.

pages.name: Part 1: Faltering Tithe
pages.text:
To call the Precinct Fortress Majoris a ‘fortress’ is a misnomer, or a staggering understatement. It is in fact the entire bottom level of the Upper Hive of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} — a maze of dark rockcrete, the headquarters of the Macharian Vigilites on Voll, and the main checkpoint through which everything and everyone travelling from Upper to Lower Hive, or vice-versa, must pass.

A flash of their passes easily gets the characters into the very heart of the Maglev Nexus and they may well marvel at how notably smooth and swift their ride is. Heavily armed @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.KTlRprKRb8XzlnAD]{Gun Servitors} and steely-eyed @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Vigilites} immediately track them as they exit the Maglift with immediate demands to see their identification. A Routine (+20) Intuition (People) Test notes that the Vigilites on guard immediately stiffen and become very polite indeed once they’ve authenticated the party’s passes. The sentries readily direct the characters on the best way to get to Block 3 if asked.

Captain Vern’s Office

The characters are stopped several times along the way to Captain Vern’s office, but a flash of their passes always sees quick salutes, and the characters are immediately waved on. Block 3 proves to effectively be a large marshalling yard where squads of Vigilites run through hand-to-hand drills and crowd control tactics.

Vern’s office is a relatively simple affair attached to the yard. It’s filled with shelves packed with dataslates. Any organisation, if it exists, must clearly be particularly arcane. Various pieces of mismatched furniture lie about the room and a massive weapons locker dominates one entire wall. Captain Vern is a veritable grox of a man, eschewing the typical Vigilite carapace armour for a sturdy-looking great coat. His dark hair is flecked with grey. He regards the characters as they enter his office with one sharp green eye and one silver-pale augmetic lens which audibly whirrs and clicks as he studies them.

Roleplaying Captain Matis Vern

Captain Vern possesses a surprisingly genial manner and welcomes the characters with no small sense of relief. He is clearly frustrated, not to mention concerned, though he does his best to keep the last emotion to himself. Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Vigilite} stat-block to represent Captain Vern if needed. If asked about his connection to the party’s Patron, he smiles and taps his augmetic eye. ‘Our mutual friend saved me from getting gutted by the Throne-cursed cur who did this.’ He picks up a dataslate, checking details as he speaks.

On The Vertexis: ‘Cults come and go in Rokarth at a fast pace. A few citizens got themselves a glimpse of our perpetrator at some point. Dressed in a black, gaunt pale face, carrying a scythe of all things. They call ‘im The Harbinger. Claim they’re loyal to the Imperium, that he’s an angel of the Emperor, come to punish the guilty. You’ll see their murals about. We erase them and eliminate anyone we catch putting them up. But they always return. Just addled scum.’

On the Killings: ‘Near as we can tell, about half a year ago is when the relevant murders began. Pretty much every night cycle since, regularly as clockwork, though the scale varies. I have a slate here for you with autopsy reports. Don’t eat afore you read. Our killer doesn’t discriminate much. No motivations that we can identify. Whole habs butchered. Few survivors. Likes blades, but not exclusively. Leaves a big mess. We thought he was a pattern killer, higher-ups didn’t much care — nobody in the Spire was getting hit. But then the sabotages began.’ 

On the Case: ‘At this point, all I’ve hit are deadwalls. We’ve had scores of savants scouring over the datapoints, but no useful connections among the victims have been discerned. However, we’re not allowed access to the Administratum’s or Imperial Navy's full records. That’s why I’m hoping you lot can shake something free. Go where I can’t. I think you should know why you’re here. It’s not just ‘cause of the Tithe. I had a squad, some of my best. Set up a trap for the Harbinger. That thing slaughtered them all, took them apart like they were nothing. Killed a squad of ten Vigilites in mere moments. I don’t know what this thing is, but like I told your boss, I don’t think it’s Human. Find this thing before more of my officers get butchered, but don’t engage it at close quarters if you can help it.’

Vern answers what questions he can, but mostly notes, ‘All in the file.’ If the characters wish to speak with one of the more coherent survivors, he arranges it for the next day. He offers them a private vox channel to contact him for support as needed, and asks to be apprised if possible. Finally, he ruefully shakes his head, saying there’s one last situation the characters have to deal with.

‘There’s a man, Administratum. Master Morlay. He’ll be waiting for you, outside the fortress, Upper Hive Gate 6. He might be useful. Maybe not. But you should probably see him, he’s got some pull.’

Grim Reading

The sheer scale of the killings listed on Captain Vern’s dataslate is daunting — well over three thousand autopsy files, including some listed as ‘corpus inconclusive’ — noting the number of victims in several incidents was undiscernible as extensive tissue breakdown due to ‘exposure to caustic elements’ had rendered differentiating victims effectively impossible with the resources available to the Vigilites’ verispex. There are clearly countless more victims than even the investigating Vigilites can account for.

It takes a successful Routine (+20) Discipline (Composure) Test for a character to force themselves to continue to read the extensive litanies of gruesome deaths listed in the reports long enough to pick up anything useful. For each level of success, they manage to understand the key details of one of the four following paragraphs:

Weaponry: Of those still intact, the bulk of the autopsies for those killed in habs indicate cause of death as deep lacerations, typically with a bladed weapon that was likely powered in some way, but not a chain weapon, as the cuts were too clean. Some died from blunt force trauma, typically from a precise blow that crushed a windpipe or a broken neck. 

Unusual Munitions: A few were shot with unusual munitions that exploded after impact. The summary report notes, with clear reluctance, that while such rounds certainly resembled those of sacred bolt weaponry, their likely calibre was not at all standard.

Toxins: The Vigilite autopsies are listed in a separate file. Several have appended toxicology reports that indicate they were exposed to a particularly virulent toxin, likely introduced via laceration with a multi-bladed weapon that readily cut through carapace armour. Several showed extreme nerve degeneration, which happened pre-mortem within mere moments of exposure. Likely exceedingly painful. One’s breastplate had been partially melted by what appeared to be a random spray of a particularly powerful corrosive compound, traces of which matched none of the many acids and corrosives found on Voll, a stunning conclusion the verispex confirmed with the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#dilaquo]{Mercator Dilaquo}.

Sabotage: A file marked as sabotage contains ten detailed industrial incidents. The common thread throughout the incidents is that, while they appeared to be accidents at first, they were all perfectly executed to cause maximum carnage. Several indicate the use of a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.99dVOsy85KLNtGTj]{Melta Bomb}, which is not at all a common or inexpensive munition.

The Master Awaits

The characters can choose whether they meet with the Master or not. A Challenging (+0) Lore (Adeptus Terra or Voll) Test notes that Master Morlay is an Adeptus Administratum Master whose main job is coordinating hive-wide festivals, chief among them Halion’s Triumph. Failure to meet up with Morlay, he considers it an insult and results in greater difficulties during @UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records}.

If the characters head to Upper Hive Gate 6, they find a slight man in once-sumptuous dark robes covered in flowing silvery script, which have seen a lot of use and appear worn. He occasionally pulls heavily on a massive, long-stemmed wooden pipe with engraved bone and metal plates. A group of rough-looking sorts, all wearing brightly scintillant jackets, surround him, acting as bodyguards.

A Routine (+20) Lore (Voll) Test recognises the distinct jackets, marking them as members of the Mercator Carnem — the Meat Guild of Voll. Sporadically, he snaps his fingers and points, causing one of these minions to lean over and relight his pipe. Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept} to represent Morlay, and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.ZIodTiyH9W5QBRU9]{Astra Militarum Trooper} to represent his guards, if required.

‘Ah, here at last. Exquisite. I am Master Nixious Morlay. I’m told you’ve come to set my festival to rights. Exacting business. I am briefly at your disposal.’ 

Morlay tends to speak in measured bursts, with unusual liberal adjective use as punctuation. A Difficult (−10) Intuition (People) Test reveals that he is very worried, though he conceals it well. Morlay asks the characters if they are aware of the supreme importance of @UUID[.GjnFA1lCGKEla9yA#halions-triumph]{Halion’s Triumph} and relays various details about it, including that he must return to work on at once. This serves as his preamble to offering his services in assisting with this ‘vexatious affair.’ 

What Morlay offers is effectively 2 @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#temporary-influence]{Temporary Influence} with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, particularly useful if the characters have no such Influence with that Faction among their members. But the cost of invoking Morlay’s Influence is that the Master knows exactly what sorts of questions the characters are asking, what they learned, and he expects regular updates on their progress with the case. He can also offer the services of his Mercator Carnem allies if the characters feel they need some muscle; however, the Meat Guild’s members ultimately answer to Morlay — which may be a problem for the party once the Master decides it is time for the characters to move on.

Characters who take Morlay up on the offer are given a copy of his personal sigil and a vox channel by which he can be reached. He requests regular reports of their progress. He looks visibly put out if they decline his offer, noting, ‘Superlative, to be so gifted at your work.’ He reacts by withdrawing in a huff but sets his Mercator Carnem agents to monitor the characters’ movements and cause them further trouble during @UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records}.

pages.name: Part 2: Strange Patterns
pages.text:
After what they’ve learned during the first part of the adventure, the characters can attempt to follow up on these leads:

  • Connections between the various victims of the Harbinger may be found if the characters can study the voluminous records held within the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} Censorium.

  • They may wish to investigate @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Voidport Records surrounding the time roughly corresponding with the Harbinger’s first kills looking for anomalies.

  • They may have taken Captain Vern up on his offer to interrogate a survivor of one of the Harbinger’s attacks the following day.

  • They may wish to seek out a less Vigilite-slanted view of the Vertexis.

Various pieces of information that can help identify what the Harbinger might be trying to achieve may emerge during these investigations, though learning any given piece of information won’t tell the characters the full story. After a day or two spent investigating, Captain Vern invites the characters to inspect the gruesome aftermath of a fresh Harbinger massacre at the @UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV#the-shattered-hab]{Shattered Hab}.

To the Censorium

The @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} Censorium is a heavily reinforced rockcrete tomb high in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Upper Hive, filled with a staggering array of data towers and cogitator arrays. All information, important or otherwise, concerning Voll’s citizenry is held here. The air is thick and charged, filled with wafts of incense, sacred oils, and redolent of ozone. Minor scribes with cloths continually wipe away condensation from scrolls, dataslates, and the sweat of their superior’s brows as servitors bearing censers of blessed waters slowly walk in preassigned patterns leaving pockets of brief respite from the humidity in their wake.   

Access to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} Censorium is heavily restricted and the characters need a measure of Influence with the Adeptus Administratum of 1 or better to access the facility. If the party lacks Influence with the Adeptus Administratum, they can still choose to take Master Morlay up on his offer.

Presuming the characters gain access to the Censorium, they are assigned a Curator to assist them in their research. All data within the Censorium is encrypted with cyphers and impossible to access or understand without assistance (unless a character has the Linguistics (Cypher) Specialisation). The characters’ liaison is Curator Adjen Sablik, a young woman with symbols from different ancient languages tattooed about her eyes in a light shade of blue ink. Her arms hold augmetic auto quills which can snap forward and incase her hands. She constantly taps her fingers, whether in or out of the quills, the sound changing depending on whether her fingers are encased or not. She is delighted by trivial information and fascinated by weapons of all sorts. Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept} stat-block to represent her if required.

The character’s success in their search for information is ultimately dictated by how well they interact with Curator Sablik. Have them chat with her for a while and take note of exactly what questions they ask. All characters present should make a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Inquiry or Charm) Test. Remember to add the characters’ highest Administratum Influence as an SL bonus. It takes several hours of cogitating till Curator Sablik comes back with the following, depending on the highest SL achieved:

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 or more SL): Looking past the high-scale massacres, in cases where only single or handfuls of victims were recorded, Curator Sablik has found a tenuous familial connection. One that stretches back for centuries, but it is there almost every time. What’s more, she spotted that many of the records had recently been accessed, within the last year, but whoever had done so had somehow managed to erase their identity from the data towers, a supposedly impossible feat.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): A considerable number of the victims are distantly related, though sometimes those connections are several generations old and not apparent. A fair third or more don’t appear to have any relation to the others.

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): Some of the victims appear to be related, but there are so many, and contained within an old sector of the hive, that it is hard to say if this is merely a minor statistical anomaly or something more meaningful.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The Curator flatly states that she does not have the time to deal with their query, but logs it for non-priority processing. Unless the characters force her hand by invoking a higher authority, she estimates the query would take over 14 standard Terran years to process.

With a Marginal Success or better, if any of the characters ask Curator Sablik if she knows why most victims would come from one portion of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, she thinks for a moment. Then she says, ‘Oh, that’s standard hive population sedentism, isn’t it?’ She goes on to explain that, unless recruited into the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum} or @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Navis Imperialis}, most born within Voll’s hives tend to spend their entire lives in the vicinity of their birth. This behaviour is actively encouraged by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum}, making many aspects of population measurement far easier. If the characters don’t make the connection themselves, she explains that, if all the victims are related to a specific set of families, it makes some sense that they would all come from one region of the hive.

If the characters ask Curator Sablik if she can locate others with the same genetic connections she’s already found, she chuckles and says, ‘Yes, but there are literally millions of them. The greater majority of which do seem to reside within the eastern Windswept Buttress. Nobody calls it that but us Curators, though.’

Rokarth Voidport Records

A hive as massive as @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} holds many secrets, few of which are easily discovered; however, there is a specific collection point where all comings and goings to the hive, along with logged records of unusual activity, are stored: the Void Buttress. The Void Buttress is Voll’s primary planetside voidport. It is utterly massive, almost a secondary spire unto itself. Its profile was built to put one in the mind of the Imperial Aquila. All legal, and quite a few illegal, imports and exports of the planet Voll pass through the Void Buttress. Portions of the Void Buttress connect to every level of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, chiefly to enable the movement of goods and passengers. The characters have likely all passed through some level of the Void Buttress at some point in their lives.

It is a matter of tradition and practical history that the Navis Imperialis controls the Void Buttress, as it does the corresponding voidport in high orbit above Voll. All citizens who wish to access the records of the Void Buttress can technically put in a request at one of its many service offices that exist on nearly every level; however, without some degree of Imperial Fleet Influence, their query is likely an exhausting endeavour just to file correctly and could take a great deal of time to get even a succinct answer, possibly years in some cases.

If the characters have sufficient Influence to expedite their query, proceed to @UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV#data-discourse]{Data Discourse}. If not, they can acquire @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#temporary-influence]{Temporary Influence}. The easiest way comes from the eminently bribable Port Ensign Novus of Void Buttress Station SW9 (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.pXsZLEawZr8Tf8Ym]{Armsman}n stat-block to represent him). If the characters find themselves rebuffed at another service office, they are directed here with a wink by a helpful citizen who overhears their queries. 

Located in the lowest levels of the Upper Hive, Station SW9 is far from busy, and its only attendant, Ensign Novus, has little to occupy his time. The Port Ensign is a lanky, affable data clerk fond of whistling void shanties and imbibing illicitly distilled beverages. A Routine (+20) Rapport (Charm or Inquiry) Test lets a character determine that a 100 solar bribe is more than enough to secure his assistance, and an effective +2 @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.qxkAEAcB9xAl56Xa#temporary-influence]{Temporary Influence} with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Navy}. A failure increases the cost of the bribe to 300 solars, though Novus is quite willing to take any useful equipment or other goods in place of hard currency.

Data Discourse

The characters doubtlessly want any information on anomalous data reported at the Void Buttress circa 5 to 6 months ago (anything unusual, odd comings and goings, weird reports, etc.) To this, the clerk notes that they want an ‘Archivium Petition Rh-49ex, with an expedited stamp, I should think’. The clerk notes that they expect the inquiry to fail, as the characters don’t have enough specific data for the cogitators.

At present, they are unfortunately correct. There are hundreds of thousands of data entries that match the open parameters of the characters query. The clerk states that if the characters can find any unusual signals, codes, or specific incidents that would’ve been logged, that would help the cogitators narrow in on the details of more useful events. 

The clerk is willing to help the characters once again after they have more information to go on. Their aid will become far more useful during @UUID[.5GjYiCc0FBtc8dhc]{Part 4: Old Records}.

The Survivor

If the characters take Captain Vern up on his offer to meet with a survivor of one of the Harbinger’s attacks, he gives them the coordinates of a Vigilite Bastion located in the upper portion of the Lower Hive and a time for the following day that roughly corresponds to an hour or so past the Second Shift. 

This particular Vigilite Bastion was once an unsanctioned bar. It eventually drew the attention of the Vigilites and was shut down, then repurposed and reinforced due to its advantageous position. Vigilites and their combative @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} charges come and go, with few sparing the characters more than a passing glance until they present themselves within the public processing chamber. A sullen Vigilite Sergeant directs traffic from behind a very long table reminiscent of the bar it once was. If the characters mention Captain Vern or they’re here to see the survivor, recognition flits across the Sergeant’s scowl. He jerks a nod towards a corridor and directs the group back to a series of interrogation chambers deep in the interior of the building. 

A Vigilite named Kairn greets the characters outside the interrogation chambers and tells them that Citizen Sorvic is officially no longer under suspicion. She also notes that she passed her confessional assessment by the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} and is to be released, despite Kairn's protests, having been found among the bodies of a half dozen dead gangers.

Marta Sorvic

Marta Sorvic sits beneath a harsh light at a heavily pocked and scarred metal table. She wears the simple yellow-white fatigues of a detainee, and her skin is reddened, almost raw. An Easy (+40) Lore (Voll) Test reveals this is a sign of having undergone recent decontamination protocols, standard practice for those detained for questioning by the Vigilites. Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.RsIGQ61VYTusa8TR]{Imperial Citizen} stat-block to represent her.

If Sorvic ever possessed any spark of defiance towards Imperial authority, it has all but been snuffed out. The characters may approach Marta Sorvic in several ways. She is reticent to talk, but a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Charm or Inquiry) Test can convince her to open up. Alternatively, the characters may attempt to intimidate her into speaking by making a Difficult (−10) Presence (Intimidation) Test or displaying some effigy of high authority. Sorvic answers their questions if the latter path is chosen, but is left a sobbing wreck by this approach.

If either Test fails, it takes several hours to extract the information from Sorvic, if the characters have the patience for it. In either case, Sorvic eventually recalls to them what she saw. 

Sorvic admits that she is a recent arrival to the area, having come up from the southern sectors of the hive in search of better opportunities. So far, this has not worked out well for her. Sorvic explains that she was a tag-along to a gang meeting, one called to discuss matters of tribute and territory. Everything was going well until ‘that thing’ attacked the assembled gangers. Sovic states that the Harbinger didn’t have a pale face, as some have claimed. Instead, it wore a pale mask, the details of which she could barely see, as the habway where the meeting took place was intentionally drowned in darkness. However, she clearly remembers its eyes, which glowed ‘red, like a terrible fire, but they turned an acid blue when they fell on me’.

If asked about gathered @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionists}, Sorvic is reticent to give too much detail. She explains that the gang was small, mostly made up of locals from a single family, the Zovols, and far from influential. If pressed for details, she admits to various small-time illegal activities in which she was tangentially involved — this is useless to the investigation, but does lead to Vigilite Kairn sweeping into the interrogation room once the characters have finished. The additional ‘confessions’ extracted from Sovic are sufficient to rescind the results of her previous confessional assessment, and the unfortunate woman is dragged away in manacles.

Attempting to investigate the Zovols leads to a literal dead end, as the minor gang has been totally wiped out. Beyond the information above, Sorvic has nothing else left to give.

The Vertexis

The characters may wish to investigate the Vertexis more, especially since the Vigilites all but dismiss them as an irrelevant cult. Allow each character involved to make a Test, and ensure each receives a different snippet of information. Asking after the group in drinking establishments, hive markets, and worship gatherings requires a Difficult (−10) Rapport (Inquiry) Test with these results:

  • Astounding Success (+5 SL or more): The characters have a chance meeting with a Sister Hospitaller of the Order of Searing Purity. She notes that she knows little of the Vertexis. Still, on the several occasions that she has had dealings with them, each time, they acted utterly awestruck by members of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum}, prostrating themselves and refusing to even look directly at priests.

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 to +4 SL): The characters meet a ganger who claims to have witnessed the Vertexis attack and kill a guild-bonded bounty hunter. He states that they tried to keep to the shadows before the attack, then hurled firebombs while opportunistically shooting. The group gains 1 Superiority in combat against the Vertexis, during the upcoming ambush in @UUID[.d03FcrEvHxHGZlE9]{Part 3: Ragged Faith}.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): The characters find a few citizens willing to discuss the Vertexis. Some think they’re harmless, just broken. A few think they are far more dangerous than they appear, but fortunately, not very well organised. The characters are directed to a newly painted mural, which frequently appears not long after a Harbinger attack. It depicts a shadowy figure with alabaster white skin, glaring red eyes, and wielding a harvest-thresher style blade above a caption which reads ‘His jugement is neer.’ 

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): The characters hear nothing as the citizens they meet are too fearful of the Harbinger and his disciples. Many tell them it is better not to talk about them, and so draw their attention.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The characters hear nothing as the citizens of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} have grown too fearful of the Harbinger and his disciples. Worse, the Vertexis learn that the characters have connections to the Vigilites and are asking after them. During the ambush in the following @UUID[.d03FcrEvHxHGZlE9]{Part 3: Ragged Faith}, a number of extra Vertexis equal to the number of characters attack them on the street alongside the Harbinger instead of waiting in the shadows to watch their angel finish the characters off.

The Shattered Hab

After the characters have explored several leads, when they are tired at the end of a working cycle and what approximates late evening in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}, Captain Vern sends them a short message — whether via vox or a courier, depending on the circumstances and where they are staying — requesting that they join him to inspect the aftermath of a Harbinger massacre.

As they still have priority access to the Maglev Nexus, it only takes about twenty minutes for the group to descend into the Lower Hive. Still, it is over an hour’s travel through long halls filled with teeming crowds of workers before they reach their destination. The cramped tunnels are lit by heavily flickering lumens, throwing harsh shadows. A hive rain slowly drifts down, smelling of rotten mud, and it burns the nostrils of those unprotected by respirators or filtration plugs.

New Massacre

The hab level they seek is one amid reclamation from damage incurred during a hive-quake several years ago, known locally as the Heap. Due to the collapse of a macro-support column, a portion of the levels above collapsed almost entirely into this one, and the merged debris of the two has become a twisted warren of tunnels, chambers, ruined machinery and partially crushed equipment.

Reclamation has been slow, but this hasn’t stopped former inhabitants and less scrupulous looters from trying to recover some of the valuables left inside. Within the crushed ceramite and plasteel of the Heap, a quiet, forgotten war is fought in cramped tunnels and half-excavated chambers over the paltry valuables left behind in the collapse. Locals are used to the occasional muffled gunshot or distant explosion that can be heard within, and know to watch for further collapses should the violence get out of hand. 

Today, however, is unusually quiet. Captain Vern waits by a collection of construction and mining equipment, a squat burning Lho-stick in his hand. Two @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.GuqQhiqch248agDB]{Vigilites} flank one of the larger entrances to the Heap. A successful Routine (+20) Intuition (People) Test indicates that all three are deeply rattled. Vern nods to the characters, then shakes his head and wipes a hand over his face.

‘Reclaimators will be here in another hour. I ordered it left undisturbed for you to see.’

If the characters have questions about the Heap, Vern explains in detail, glad for the distraction from the more immediate topic at hand. He finds any excuse not to accompany the characters immediately inside, as do the other Vigilites. 

Several large chambers have been the site of recent reclamation work and an even more recent slaughter. Every surface is covered in blood, pieces of mutilated bodies scattered across the interior. The primary chamber is brightly lit by lumens and tripod-mounted Stablights that the Vigilites have set up. They make the gore coating the walls and lining the ceiling in long sprayed arcs all too visible. Several nearby chambers are in a similar state, and those who venture deeper into the Heap finds lone victims scattered here and there in similar states.

Anyone who enters the Heap must make a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Composure) Test. Failure means that the Difficulty of any other Tests they take while inside is increased by one step. It is up to the Players to decide whether their characters that failed begin weeping, void the contents of their stomach, or are stricken by uncontrollable shaking.

New Clues

Captain Vern eventually enters and explains what the Vigilites have learned so far:

  • From the makeshift uniforms, scattered weapons, and some tattoos, it appears that the victims were looters, who Vern considers little better than @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} gangers.

  • There are more dead than can easily be counted, but it would appear that any looters not killed are lying low, as the Heap has been all but abandoned.

  • The locals claim to have heard and seen nothing, despite what must have been a substantial battle.

Have any character who passed the previous Discipline (Composure) Test to make a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test. Whoever achieves the most SL spots the remains of a broken @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-items.Item.V2OgwHeEr3qpTbBy]{stummer} in an alcove. It appears Imperial in origin, but not standard. A Tech-priest can glean from its design that it originates from the Segmentum Solar. It also seems to have been crushed during a struggle.

Characters can make a Challenging (+0) Logic (Investigation) Test to search the hab (remember to increase the difficulty if they failed the Discipline (Composure) Test earlier), revealing the following:

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 or more SL): Judging by the clotting of the gore, this massacre happened approximately two days ago. Viscera and various limbs were scattered on purpose, post-mortem. There is no discernible pattern, but there is an underlying sense of controlled rage in the butchery.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): A powered sword was the primary weapon used in the killings. A few were done with a multi-bladed weapon as well, some variant of a power claw, perhaps. The victims were mainly caught unaware. Several were killed at the same time. The assailant was incredibly skilled — every blow was precise.

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): A powered blade was used, most likely a sword. The killings seem random.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The assailant used a bladed weapon and was incredibly strong — other details are lost amidst the slaughter.

Vern notes that no witnesses have come forward. The bodies were discovered during a routine search of the hab complex by Vigilite compliance teams. If shown the broken stummer, Vern smiles grimly. ‘Ah, that’s how the deviant stays so quiet.’

pages.name: Part 3: Ragged Faith
pages.text:
As the characters leave the devastated hab, they see Vertexis-style graffiti marked on an opposing hab wall, the sinister figure of the pale-faced Harbinger looming over crumbling statuary with an inerudite inscription that reads, ‘Judgement is coming!’ 

Harbinger Ambush
