As the weary characters make their way back towards the Maglev Nexus through the crowded habs and walkways of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Lower Hive, @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.47e5e8pz6cKrei1w]{the Harbinger} and a particularly fanatic group of his @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BNzIELnXHo5A5LGP]{Vertexis} followers attempt to end the characters’ sinful existences and stop their blasphemous investigation into their righteous activities via an ambush.

Describe the habway the characters are navigating along, noting the flowing crowds that all appear functionally identical, all dressed in almost the same grey and brown utilitarian garb. The drainage canal flows beside them, and the sharp calls of commissary vendors holding aloft metal sticks spiked with questionable meats from the risen areas above. There is a continual murmur of the horde and the scraping, gritty shuffle of countless muddy feet. The lumens flicker, and the shadows are long. 

Ask the characters to make a Difficult (−10) Awareness (Sight) or Intuition (Surroundings) Test to see if they notice the upcoming ambush and whether they are @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.YEIzXenjBxa3GlTQ#surprise]{Surprised}:

  • Impressive Success or better (+3 or more SL): The character notices the slight thinning of the crowd around them as menacing figures appear on the walkways and the covered bridge above them. They are not Surprised and have the time to take an Action before combat begins.

  • Marginal Success or better (+0 to +2 SL): The character perceives the crowd thinning about them. They are not Surprised when combat begins.

  • Marginal Failure or worse (0 to −2 SL): The character does not notice the Vertexis gathering to attack and is Surprised when combat begins.

  • Impressive Failure or worse (−3 SL or less): The character does not notice the Vertexis gathering to attack and is Surprised when combat begins. When the Harbinger leaps down to attack, the character must make a Difficult (−10) Discipline (Fear) Test or become Frightened of the grim figure.

There are a number of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.BNzIELnXHo5A5LGP]{Vertexis Cultists}, equal to the number of characters plus 2, in addition to the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.47e5e8pz6cKrei1w]{Harbinger}. If the characters failed badly in trying to learn more about the Vertexis, add two more Vertexis Cultists to the pack.

The Vertexis are nearly identical to the crowd surrounding the characters, except they have makeshift skull masks covering their faces, all made from pieces of flat bone, skulls, or servo-skulls. They wield simple fire bombs, makeshift weapons, and poorly manufactured and maintained autoguns. The Harbinger appears exactly as the characters have been led to believe — a menacing figure swathed in black with a stark white face, gleaming red augmetic eyes, and a crude but effective-looking powered scythe.

Zone 1: Drainage Canal

The characters start in this Zone. For the first two rounds of combat, Zone 1 counts as Difficult Terrain due to the surrounding crowds, but the crowd also provides Light Cover. By the third round, these Environmental Traits cease as much of the crowd has fled. Characters can fall into the open drainage canal — they can make a Difficult (−10) Athletics (Swimming) Test to escape before the current pulls them away. Characters can also make a Difficult (−10) Athletics (Might) Test to jump across to the other side safely.

Zone 2: Northern Overhang

This Zone is strewn with market stalls offering trinkets, simple goods, and quick bites to eat. The area is Difficult Terrain due to the clutter but it also provides ample Medium Cover to characters within. Stray gunshots can ignite gas tanks and make holes in the surrounding pipeworks, causing Minor Hazards to those nearby. Half the Vertexis Cultists retreat towards this area if they become overpowered.

Zone 3: Southern Overhang

This Zone mirrors Zone 2 (Northern Overhang), with the same Features and Traits, except it also features a hidden escape hatch into the hive waterways. It can be found by making a Challenging (+0) Awareness (Sight) Test or witnessing one of the Vertexis Cultists escaping. The other half of the Vertexis Cultists retreat towards this area if they become overpowered.

Zone 4: Walkways

Two wide walkways join Zones 2 and 3 together. The Vertexis Cultists begin their attacks from these walkways, hurling their firebombs onto the habway below. Characters have Light Cover in these Zones if characters in Zone 1 below attack them. Characters who fall from these walkways land in the Drainage Canal below.

Tricks and Tactics

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5Bx7K8k9VgjOZmA4]{Adeptus Ministorum} characters gain Advantage if they forcefully confront the Vertexis Cultists with a Presence (Intimidation) Test. If they succeed at the Test with an Impressive result or better (+3 or more SL), the characters immediately gain a point of Superiority.

The Vertexis Cultists begin their ambush by hurling fire bombs down on the characters from above. As the burning fuel of the bombs causes the screaming crowds to flee, the Harbinger leaps down to finish off the characters. The Vertexis aim to pick off stray characters from above while their angel fights the wicked.

The Harbinger is a fanatic and will never retreat. He fights to the death. If the Harbinger falls, any remaining Vertexis immediately break and flee from the scene.

Inspecting his weaponry, the Harbinger’s scratch-built powered scythe reveals to be a blasphemous device to any Tech-Priest. Its origins are unclear, and any interrogation of the self-proclaimed Harbinger results only in claims that it was a gift from the God-Emperor.

Never a Vigilite when you need one…

This ambush could rapidly turn deadly if the characters are not particularly combat-oriented. If they took up Master Morlay’s offer, they may already have Meat Guild Enforcers near to hand who surpass the odds (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcer} stat-block to represent them). If not, after one or more characters have gone down, the Mercator Carnem shows its hand, and their enforcers suddenly arrive to deal with the Harbinger. Morlay thanks the characters for their efforts in ‘routing out this mendacious scourge’ and then dismisses them — permanently, in his view.

pages.name: Part 4: Old Records
pages.text:
The news of the Harbinger’s fall swiftly moves through @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}, strongly reinforced by the fact that for the first time in close to half a year, the nightly killings cease.

However, the characters might notice that the Harbinger’s body does not conform to all the information the characters may have gathered on his activities. His only weapon was a single-bladed powered scythe, and no toxins were found on him. Indeed, the open ambush was completely atypical of how he has operated thus far. Any captured Vertexis are in mourning, for they swear that he was the Harbinger, and they all believe it, declaring it so even under the duress the Vigilites put them to.

Within two days of the ambush, Captain Vern calls the characters to his office, where he awaits them alongside Master Morlay. Depending on the nature of their relationship with the Master and the circumstances of the Harbinger’s fall, the characters may be sincerely congratulated and perhaps even rewarded, or sneeringly dismissed. Morlay expects them to move on and pointedly ignores any notion that the Harbinger hasn’t been permanently dealt with. With that, he leaves to attend to festival business, which is now less than a week away.

If the characters insist the true Harbinger hasn’t been dealt with, Captain Vern believes them, but his hands are tied. With the deaths seemingly stopped, he suggests the characters must quickly act if they intend to investigate further, as Morlay will soon cut off their access.

The Shanty Man’s Connection

As the characters plot their next moves, presuming they dealt with him during @UUID[.hcHx5BUaaQ2iISkV#rokarth-voidport-records]{Rokarth Voidport Records}, a courier arrives with a missive from Port Ensign Novus of Void Buttress Station SW9. 

‘I met someone you all really need to talk to.’

Once the characters reach his office, Ensign Novus tells them that a Tech-Priest approached him with an unusual story they should hear. Presuming the characters agree, he’ll swiftly arrange for her to join them. If the characters never contacted Ensign Novus, they could be approached by a different Contact who knows the Tech-Priest, or Captain Vern might direct Loga Binary-46 their way.

Loga Binary-46 proves to be a woman with gleaming, golden-hued augmetic eyes. The lower portion of her face is a permanent augmetic respirator. Her voice is surprisingly pleasant, and she speaks softly, albeit with a distinct metallic reverberation. She wears the distinct red robes of the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. Several mechadendrites smoothly stir about her. (Use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.rilaQaBPslIRzGco]{Tech-Priest} stat-block to represent her).

Roleplaying Loga Binary-46

Though it is considered somewhat gauche to admit to strong emotions within the Adeptus Mechanicus, Loga Binary-46 is very concerned with the implications of the pattern of events she has observed thus far. Her mechadendrites move in time with her voice, stopping suddenly and unnervingly when she is surprised or intent.

‘Genial greetings. I am Loga Binary-46, servant of the Omnissiah. Several anomalous events have transpired, which Ensign Novus suggests require social interaction between us. Ongoing analysis indicates a series of misappropriations from various Adeptus Mechanicus holdings within Hive Rokarth. Several were highly volatile explosives capable of causing substantial damage, along with devices used for remote detonation. Common data point — each theft used a high-level override code over six centuries old, and one not usually seen on Voll.’

Ensign Novus grins and produces a dataslate. ‘The exact same code used to gain access to Hive Rokarth through an exterior hatch, just shy of 6 months ago, not long after a small impact was detected in the vicinity of the hatch.’

‘Ensign Novus tells me these events have congruence and will be relevant to you. Query – is his analysis correct?’

Loga Binary-46 is willing to answer several clarifying questions, but will otherwise raise an eyebrow and ask ‘Relevance?’ to any other unrelated queries. If asked what she does for the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, she notes that she is one of the Machine God’s Curators, offering no further explanation. If asked what ‘substantial damage’ translates to, her mechadendrites stop still, and after a pause, she responds, ‘Extensive damage to ancient and revered apparatus would occur, including a significant reduction in the locally available workforce. Importing and retraining replacements would take weeks.’

Loga asks only a few direct questions — if she is satisfied that the characters can aid her in averting disaster, that is sufficient. She knows where the hatch is located. It will take considerable time to travel to it as it corresponds to an exterior portion of the lower-Upper Hive, nearly as far from the Maglev Nexus as is possible within @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}. The Tech-Priest lifts a hand, and a servitor enters, bearing a gleaming cog axe, which she accepts. ‘Query: shall we undertake an excursion?’

The Damaged Pod

It takes a full five hours to reach the hatch Ensign Novus identified. Any characters who intend to go out onto @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} exterior to see what they can find may want to acquire protective gear beyond what they usually carry. The access point is a maintenance hatch that opens onto Voll's caustic environment, which the characters can easily open as they have the codes. Journeying into the mild caustic haze requires a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Endurance) Test. Characters that fail are subject to the effects of exposure to a @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.UaRHLqZ99zmg7AeE#exposure]{noxious environment}. Any character without protective eyewear (or augmetic eyes) has Disadvantage on all Awareness (Sight) Tests in this environment. 

It takes some time to locate the source of Ensign Novus’ impact site, as it has been hidden under a large swatch of chemically treated covering removed from elsewhere on the hive. A successful Difficult (−10) Awareness (Sight) Test soon notes faint scorch marks and scraped metal, eventually leading to the partially camouflaged orbital drop pod. Failure on the Test eventually reveals the pod, but it takes time, necessitating a Difficult (−10) Fortitude (Endurance) Test and potentially more substantial exposure damage.

The drop pod is clearly damaged, with a partially scorched and ravaged exterior. Its size indicates that it likely held only a single occupant. Loga Binary-46 immediately moves to study the pod. Though she readily accepts the assistance of any @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus} characters, she pointedly stops anyone else from assisting her. One of her mechadendrites begins asserting various devices into the pod, and her fingers tap across different points.

‘Analysis: This is one of the most advanced of these blessed devices I have ever encountered. It is a cryo-crypt as well as a drop pod. The communication module of this vessel is heavily damaged — its occupant received orders to activate, but a second message is stuck within its data circuits. That second message’s transmittal code originates from Voll, directly from the Crystalline Reflectory, sent at the highest priority. This incept date… the message was broadcast approximately five hundred and sixty years ago.’

A Challenging (+0) Lore (Macharian Sector) Test reveals that the message originates squarely within the time of the Macharian Heresy, several decades after the founding of Voll. Loga Binary-46 notes that the data circuits have sadly degraded, leaving the message garbled. But she has successfully recorded the complete transmittal code, meaning that, in theory, the message can be retrieved from the Crystalline Reflectory. 

Other duties call her, but the Tech-Priest passes the message’s code information to the characters on a dataslate and asks the party to inform her of what they discover.

Interception

If the characters are not careful to keep their ongoing investigation quiet, Master Morlay eventually sends a group of Meat Guild Enforcers to speak with them (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.gQxTENJSdTQTVfDM]{Enforcer} stat-block to represent them). If they’ve had a decent working relationship with Morlay, it is a pointed warning and a strong suggestion to wrap their affairs up and move on. If not, the enforcers attack, intending to beat the characters to a pulp, but not kill them. If the characters still don’t take the hint, two days before Halion’s Triumph, a whole squad of Meat GuildEnforcers attack them on the street with the intent of capturing them and imprisoning them until the festival is over, so they can’t interfere further.

The View from Above

Travelling to the Crystalline Reflectory is likely an unusual experience for the characters, as it is located within @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} Spires. Once they’ve left the Maglev Nexus, the characters immediately become aware of how open and comparatively quiet the spaces are. There is little thrum of machinery in the spires, no loud vox hailers, no distant screaming. The people here are engaged in business while dressed in casual finery that lower hivers can barely conceive of. All the buildings seem opulent, though careful study notes time-worn cracks in many.

Characters of a less affluent appearance are stopped and questioned by the most immaculately dressed Vigilites they’ve ever met. Though they may have a right to be there with the correct identification, the Vigilite makes clear they should be about their business and then swiftly leave.

The Crystalline Reflectory is a gleaming spike that stands out even amidst the opulence of the Spires, but something about the building's alignment causes a headache if it is gazed at directly for too long. It is an open secret that all the interior walls are said to be lined with psychically active crystalline lattices, enabling the Astropaths within to receive and send Astropathic transmissions more efficiently.

Access to the Crystalline Reflectory is relatively easy, as they routinely accept commissions for messages from the kind of individuals that would have access to the Spires; however, once the characters request access to records supposedly sent centuries ago, they are ushered into a consultation with Adept Callidon Miers (use the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.vds8HRa533wcv1Pq]{Administratum Adept} stat-block to represent him).

Adept Miers’ age is difficult to tell, for his features have a timeless quality. His eyes are hidden behind a deep red scarf, covered with brightly coloured whorls of turquoise and magenta that slowly flow over the surface of the cloth as the characters meet with him. He occasionally tilts his head and cocks it at an angle, apparently listening to something the characters cannot hear. He chooses his words thoughtfully, and though he speaks softly, his voice echoes uncannily.

If the characters have an Influence of 2 or more with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.OjmVcVX5lv76LsvL]{Adeptus Astra Telepathica}, or one among them is a psyker, the discussion goes smoothly, and Adept Miers accompanies them to the Crystalline Reflectory’s Transept Vault to help retrieve what they seek. If they do not, he still ultimately helps them, but he requires their assistance with a future matter. In short, the party would owe the Adeptus Astra Telepathica a favour. 

The Transept Vault

After passing the vox transmittal code, the characters recovered from the downed pod through a cogitator and a consultation with a data crypt, Adept Miers leads the characters through various well-appointed hallways while pointedly ignoring the screams and shrieks that occasionally emerge from behind closed doors. Eventually, they pass down into a large hall formed of large grey blocks of stone covered with various sigils that visibly flicker out of the corner of the eye.

‘Astropathic messages are not as simple as vox transmissions. Interpreting them is more art than fact. When an Astropath receives a message, it often comes in symbols akin to a waking dream. Many will translate it into a physical medium as they strive to understand it. We seek a mural, created by Astropath Nalgi Osh well over five centuries ago — thus, it rests amidst some of the oldest records of the Crystalline Reflectory.’

In the vault, Miers pulls forth a sheet of marble-lined crystal, which slowly rolls out of the wall. Fixed upon the crystal is a painting, protected by the slight shimmer of an energy shield of some kind. Miers passes a hand over part of the marble, and the shield disappears. He solemnly takes the painting and places it upon a broad table, upon which increasingly brighter lights shine. Among the details, it features a menacing skull with glowing eyes, a man hanging from a tree, and the piece is covered in distorted text and symbols in between, except for the names ‘Interitas’ and ‘Caelius’ spelt out clearly. Show or hand your players a copy of the mural for them to analyse.

A Hard (−20) Lore (Macharian Sector) Test recalls that Marshal Surlan Caelius was a traitor who served under General Lysander. He was supposedly killed during the Macharian Heresy. Characters can make a Hard (−20) Linguistics (Cypher or High Gothic) Test to decode the symbols. Otherwise, Adept Miers can transcribe the symbols for them.

After a moment, Miers whispers ‘Throne.’ He pauses for a long moment, looking visibly upset. ‘This seems to be an official missive from the Officio Assassinorum. These red symbols are code, rescinding a kill order against a man named Caelius and his entire household. It instructs the assassin Interitas to… unclear… suspend its operations, I think… and await further orders.’

He allows the characters to take picts of the mural, but won’t let the physical artefact leave the Crystalline Reflectory. He specifically requests not to know anything more about this matter and escorts them out with haste. He also provides them with the translated decoded shutdown command: ‘Unit Shutdown: Primus Sanctus Red’ adding the vital fact that it must be spoken aloud to Interitas.

pages.name: Part 5: The Apocalypse Nears
pages.text:
When the characters descend from the Spires, it is approximately three days till Halion’s Triumph begins. Once the characters have had a chance to talk about their next moves, a messenger servo-skull appears with a message from their Patron.

‘Your mission’s parameters have changed. You must do what you can to retrieve the Harbinger alive. I have assembled a strike team to aid you. They are en route to you but will arrive in approximately seven days. The Emperor protects.’

Bringing in the Tech-Priest

If the characters take what they’ve learned to Loga Binary-46, she registers as pleased. She explains to the characters that she and some colleagues have determined that the stolen remote detonators have signals that can be interfered with, in part because the density of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} architecture dilutes their signal. 

‘The information you have gathered suggests the assassin will strike at Halion’s Triumph. We must disrupt his signal. In this matchless opportunity, he will be forced to activate his explosives manually, even as you are compelled to directly confront him to input the cancellation order and terminate his mission. A pleasing symmetry; the Omnissiah approves.’

She assists the characters in determining the most likely spots where explosives would need to be placed to cause the most harm at the Halion’s Triumph commemoration in eastern @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. She employs numerous Adeptus Mechanicus’ devices, many of which she does not discuss openly, to search for the Harbinger in those areas. 

The night before the commemoration, she sends a vox message to the characters, informing them she has spotted the assassin moving stealthily at great speed and knows with only a 3% chance of error where he will be located on the morrow to set off his explosives manually.

‘May probability skew in our favour. Ave Omnissiah.’

Confronting the Eversor

The site Loga Binary-46 has determined as the most likely location where the characters can confront the assassin, is a maintenance corridor within the upper sections of the Lower Hive. The corridor is under three meters wide, its sides lined with piping and various inscrutable machinery. A Challenging (+0) Tech (Engineering) Test reveals that the bulk of the machinery is for air regulation and power dispersal, but also that the corridor underlies one of the main retention walls, which supports the eastern Windswept Buttress.

The information the characters have gathered about Interitas during the course of Implacable means they likely gain 1 Superiority against him for Know Thy Foe. You should also determine if the party has garnered more @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.3j1kargHBeCTssE7#gaining-superiority-before-combat]{Superiority} for the fight ahead.

No level of stealth affords the characters the opportunity to catch the assassin unaware due to a device he carries called a Sentinel Array — but they won’t know that. Characters working with the Tech-Priest have a good idea when the assassin is about to arrive due to ongoing vox warnings. That still doesn’t lessen the impact as he looms out of the shadows of the hive.

Confronting the terrifying presence of an Eversor Assassin requires a Hard (−20) Discipline (Fear) Test. It also takes a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Composure) Test to speak Interitas’ mission retraction orders clearly and calmly. If the speaker doesn’t know High Gothic, they make this Test with Disadvantage. Failure means they must try again in the following round, presuming they are still alive, as Interitas immediately shifts to attack anyone trying to give him a shutdown order.

@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.Tb2PzBCvBZiVSKPD]{Eversor Interitas} is more than capable of slaughtering all the characters — fighting defensively is almost certainly their best option. Echoing gunfire in an enclosed corridor prevents the assassin from being able to hear what is being said to him clearly. This does not necessarily prevent him from shooting — the best way to stop that is to engage him in melee combat.

If the shutdown command is successfully delivered, ‘Unit Shutdown: Primus Sanctus Red’, Interitas immediately stops in his tracks — even mid-attack. He sheaths his weapons and moves for the drop pod, where he falls into a deep state of psycho-restraint.

The Coward’s Way

If the characters choose not to act and await their Patron’s strike team, on the day of Halion’s Triumph, a series of massive explosions collapse the greater part of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth's} eastern Windswept Buttress. The number of deaths is staggering, and the final number is ultimately impossible to determine. The Harbinger’s predations begin again the following evening.

Let the characters say what they choose to do, if anything, to assist the folk of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. Once the strike team arrives, they take all the information the characters have gathered, then dismiss them. It takes weeks for them to track and confront the Harbinger, and during that time, hundreds more civilians die. Their Patron is exceedingly displeased with them all, holding their failure to intervene as reprehensible cowardice.

If the Tech-Priest Loga Binary-46 ever learns the characters suspected what was coming, but did not act, they immediately lose 2 Influence with her and the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}. 

Other Solutions

The characters may have gathered enough information to confront the assassin without the Tech-Priest's assistance. The characters may have deduced some way of locating him or correctly surmised that he must be close enough for the detonation signal to carry through @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} thick architecture. In such a case, bow to the law of dramatic necessity and let them find him before he has set off the signal. If they cannot stop him one way or another within four combat rounds, he sets off the explosives, then withdraws to continue his mission the following evening.

pages.name: Aftermath
pages.text:
With Interitas rebound to his cryo pod, the party’s Patron wearily contacts the Officio Assassinorum, alerting the Assassin Temple to Interitas’ survival and presence on Voll. Their Patron orders them to scour any thought or notion of Interitas from their minds — the Officio Assassinorum is never to be spoken of again — and threatens to wipe their minds if they cannot stay their tongues. That said, Interitas is an interesting character to keep in your back pocket for future adventures — perhaps the Officio Assassinorum took the opportunity to keep Interitas on Voll, to improve their operations in the Macharian Sector. But the characters would never know this for sure.

Some NPCs the characters encountered could become valuable Contacts or Hirelings in their future adventures, such as Loga Binary-46 (if they manage to defeat Interitas with her help), Captain Matis Vern or Port Ensign Novus (who could aid the characters in gaining access to protected parts of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth}), and Curator Adjen Sablik or Adept Callidon Miers (who could help the characters with appropriate research during their future investigations).

Experience Points

All characters should earn @Reward[xp=30 reason=Implacable]{30 XP} for participating in the adventure, but if any characters achieved personal goals or fulfilled a goal for a Patron, their reward should be increased accordingly. In addition, the following experience can be awarded:

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Gathered a clue]{10 XP} for each clue gathered during Part 1. 

  • @Reward[xp=10 reason=Gathared a clue]{10 XP} for each clue gathered during Part 2.

  • @Reward[xp=20 reason=Survived the Vertexis ambush]{20 XP} for surviving the Vertexis ambush and defeating the copycat Harbinger.

  • @Reward[xp=40 reason=Confronted and shut down the Eversor Inheritas]{40 XP} for confronting and shutting down Eversor Interitas.

Influence

Award or reduce the character’s Personal Influence according to their behaviour towards the factions they have encountered — primarily the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.nYfLVXh10BKR47Kj]{Adeptus Mechanicus}, if they successfully worked with Loga Binary-46 during Parts 4 and 5, or the Macharian Vigilites (@UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}) for aiding Captain Matis Vern, or the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.HlxK2pbpx2Uio6bU]{Imperial Fleet} for dealing favourably with Port Ensign Novus. Consider altering their Influence with the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.3TtxuCzt0nNV1ysj]{Adeptus Administratum} (by extension of the Officio Assassinorum) for dealing with Interitas. However, they might not recognise this effect until they next directly deal with the Adeptus Administratum or the Officio Assassinorum.  

These increases can bleed over to their Patron’s Influences if they represented their Patron honourably or made such a gross error in judgment as to affect their Patron’s standings. Aim to award (or detract) at least one point to each character and their Patron.

Failure

If the characters fail to complete the main objectives of the adventure, Interitas is left to continue on his rampage, as noted in the @UUID[.UHtSqeiaUMvo4YMP#the-cowards-way]{Coward’s Way}. However, there are also some other points of failure to note from earlier in the adventure.

Failure to stop the Harbinger during Part 3 allows the Vertexis Cult to continue growing. They use Halion’s Triumph to wipe out more targeted citizens (with or without Interitas’s attacks to back them up), and Master Morlay won’t halt the commemorations for anything. If Interitas is dealt with, the Harbinger garners a greater cult of personality and continues their killings without proper direction. They swallow up lesser cults in @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth} to add to their ranks and continue spreading throughout the Hive, turning the lower reaches of the hive into battle zones, pitching fights between them and the Vigilites.

Failure to stop the attacks during Halion’s Triumph and the resulting loss of life cause @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Hive Rokarth's} productivity to plummet, and with it, the average citizen’s quality of life. The eastern sectors of the hive become ripe for @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist} elements to thrive, and by extension, Rokarth’s Genestealer Cult cells. As the @UUID[Compendium.impmal-starter-set.journals.JournalEntry.Vjfxkwi1rFYPnSIf.JournalEntryPage.AgChFLsZYrdMa2pS#castyx]{Castyx} Dynasty scrambles to source replacement workers from Voll’s other hives or nearby systems, the Dynasty’s control over Voll wavers, allowing other families and guilds to rise in power against them.

What’s Next?

The end of this adventure has a few loose ends that could be spun into further adventures for your party. Consider the following:

  • Captain Matis Vern approaches the characters, asking for aid to track down the remaining pockets of Vertexis Cult members strewn across the eastern sectors of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. They are still eliminating citizens, a long list of names given to them by the Harbinger before their demise. But without a leader, the Vertexis remnants are ripe to be manipulated by one of Hive Rokarth’s hidden chaos cults, or perhaps tied to the following thread. 

  • During the adventure, characters may have noticed the Harbinger’s strange Power Scythe, and its obviously tech-heresy construction. This can only mean one thing: a rogue heretek is operating on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-journals.JournalEntry.8lJW1E95hsf5Hu4K.JournalEntryPage.yspwSIQuXjVjk3NA#hive-rokarth]{Rokarth}. They offer their services to the widespread heretical cults hidden in the hive city, seeking to bolster their power and dissent against the hive’s status quo. Did they know about Interitas’s mission, the presence of the Eversor Assassin, and think the Vertexis a cult worth manipulating? The characters could once more gain the aid of Loga Binary-46 to track down this foe — the magos within Forge-fane Incalos-6 would greatly appreciate the character’s support if this heretek is dealt with swiftly and without public notice.

pages.name: Dramatis Personae
pages.text:
The party may encounter the following characters during the course of their adventure. Any other stat-blocks required to play can be found in the Imperium Maledictum Core Book, with the appropriate page number referenced in the adventure’s text.

Eversor Interitas

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.Tb2PzBCvBZiVSKPD description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

Wait, are they meant to fight that?

The short answer is — no. An Eversor Assassin is far beyond the capabilities of the average character. Their only hope is to take it by surprise (almost impossible), lure it into a trap (possible, likely suicidal), or deliver the shutdown code verbally (merely very risky) — ‘Unit Shutdown: Primus Sanctus Red’. Ideally, the players choose this final option, but at this point in the mission, they have seen several examples of how dangerous the Assassin truly is. If, knowing that, they still wish to confront this monstrous foe, you should allow them to do so. That is what Fate Points are for, after all.

The Harbinger

@Embed[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-voll-actors.Actor.47e5e8pz6cKrei1w description=top table=true style=width:70%;margin:auto;]

Vertexis Cultist
